\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}

Theorems~F and G make the collision experiment, rather than the order-two
quotient, the mathematical centre of the article.  For an isolated repeated
rate in a fixed-order sampled generalized-Erlang renewal, the stationary
binary record has a uniform Gaussian half-space experiment in the squared
separation coordinate.  The sampled fourth-order pole proves uniform
nuisance-adjusted information, the residualized score attains the one-sided
power envelope, and the finite-tail recurrence estimator and contiguity
argument match at \(N^{-1/4}\).  The two-state result is the prerequisite
special case, not the endpoint of the extension.

The deterministic marked reset turns the visible output of the constrained
D-MAP into a renewal process.  This is the source of both the explicit record
law and the low-dimensional quotient inverse.  It is also the source of the
model's fragility: a marked transition into the ready state removes the fixed
Palm restart and invalidates the renewal product used by the inverse and the
retained-cycle calculations.

The visible law determines the unordered survival pair, not the hidden labels.
The two-state fibre result makes that distinction concrete.  Away from the
exchange diagonal, weakly equivalent stochastic realizations in the
killed-reset cone form a closed arc with the two triangular rate orderings as
endpoints.  On the diagonal the arc collapses.  In higher state dimension the
\((n-1)^2\) orbit calculation applies to the minimal interior stratum and is
not a statement about the global dimension of every visible fibre.

The lettered two-state inferential statements A--E remain downstream of the
population algebra.  Theorem~C estimates the three inclusion coordinates;
Theorem~D checks the complete visible law under its stated null and alternative
classes; Theorem~E transports Theorem~C through the stable quotient chart of
Theorem~B.  Sorted roots and log-rates are ordinary delta-method consequences.
The physical-image test is a separate finite-dimensional diagnostic.  The
abstract semiparametric, moving-dimensional coupling, complete-Palm-gap split,
and projection calculations are supplementary and are not used to replace the
stationary likelihood proof in Theorems~F--G.

\subsection{Sampled-counter interpretation}

Continuous dead-time and exponential-recovery detector models motivate the
two-state parametrization
\cite{YuFessler2000,SarbaziSafariHaas2018LongDeadTime,
KrauseWalenta2025SPADRecovery}.  They do not provide the theorem object here:
continuous within-bin recovery after a click can give a marked transition into
the ready state, whereas the present D-MAP latches every click in the dead
state until the boundary.  The sampled counter is therefore an interpretation
of the constrained kernel, not an independently analysed physical system.

calendar-time scaling, and exchange-local calibration remain model-specific.
The double centring and additive projection are attributed to Bickel--Kwon. \\
\addlinespace
Regenerative CLTs, separated batches, and the multivariate delta method
\cite{Janson2024RenewalCLT,AsmussenGlynn2007,
FlegalJones2010BatchMeansSpectral}. &
Complete retained Palm cycles estimate \((r_0,r_1,r_2)\), after which the
stable quotient map gives \((p+s,ps)\). &
Theorems~C and E discharge the stopped-prefix, plug-in-centering, and quotient

\endgroup

\subsection{Sampled-counter interpretation}

Continuous dead-time and exponential-recovery detector models motivate the
two-state parametrization
\cite{YuFessler2000,SarbaziSafariHaas2018LongDeadTime,
KrauseWalenta2025SPADRecovery}.  They do not provide the theorem object here:
continuous within-bin recovery after a click can give a marked transition into
the ready state, whereas the present D-MAP latches every click in the dead
state until the boundary.  The sampled counter is therefore an interpretation
of the constrained kernel, not an independently analysed physical system.

 124: \begin{assumption}[Constrained sampled-counter D-MAP model]\label{ass:model-inference-contract-main}
 125: Fix \((\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)\in(0,\infty)^3\) and define
 126: \[
 127: p=e^{-\Gamma\Delta\tau},\qquad
 128: s=e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau},
 129: \]
 130: \[
 131: a=\int_0^{\Delta\tau}\kappa_{\mathrm r}e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}r}
 132: \bigl(1-e^{-\Gamma(\Delta\tau-r)}\bigr)\,dr,\qquad
 133: b=\int_0^{\Delta\tau}\kappa_{\mathrm r}e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}r}
 134: e^{-\Gamma(\Delta\tau-r)}\,dr .
 135: \]
 136: The record model is the two-state D-MAP with hidden states ordered as
 137: \((R,D)\) and labelled kernels
 138: \[
 139: T_0=\begin{pmatrix}p&0\\ b&s\end{pmatrix},
 140: \qquad
 141: T_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1-p\\0&a\end{pmatrix}.
 142: \]
 143: The convention is
 144: \((T_i)_{XY}=\PP(A_n=i,H_{n+1}=Y\mid H_n=X)\), the visible process
 145: \((A_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}\) is the stationary binary process generated by these
 146: kernels, and formulas on \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\) are interpreted by
 147: continuous limits.  The killed entries \(T_1(R,R)=T_1(D,R)=0\) are a structural
 148: constraint of this D-MAP, not optional boundary cases of the finite-record
 149: theorems.
 150: \end{assumption}

 152: \subsection{Scope of finite-record reports}\label{subsec:finite-record-report-scope-main}
 153: 
 154: The retained-record limits are fixed-setting asymptotic statements inside the
 155: stationary law specified in \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}.  The
 156: model, population point, complete-cycle convention, and deterministic batch
 157: sequence are fixed before the record is interpreted.  Theorems~C and D are CLT
 158: and specification-test statements, respectively; Theorem~E is the quotient
 159: delta method.  The pointwise projection example is supplementary and has no
 160: confidence-set, testing, or coverage conclusion.
 161: 
 162: The only model interpretation assumed by this contract is the latched
 163: killed-leakage sampled-counter protocol of
 164: \Cref{lem:classical-counter-kernel-construction-main}.  If the sampling
 165: interval \(\Delta\tau\) is a known design interval, the visible stationary
 166: record identifies the unordered survival-factor set
 167: \(\{p,s\}=\{e^{-\Gamma\Delta\tau},e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau}\}\) and
 168: hence the unordered numerical rate set
 169: \(\{\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}\}\).  It does not identify which member is the
 170: attempt rate and which is the recovery rate without side information.  If
 171: \(\Delta\tau\) is not treated as a known design interval, the visible law
 172: identifies only the dimensionless unordered product set
 173: \(\{\Gamma\Delta\tau,\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau\}\); the same record does
 174: not put those products on an absolute numerical rate scale.
 175: 
 176: The supplementary singular likelihood calculation observes a deterministic
 177: number of independent complete Palm gaps.  Its exact product experiment is
 178: uniform for \(z\) in compact subsets of \((0,1)\) and bounded local split
 179: \(h\), and it identifies only \(h^2\).  It does not establish an endpoint
 180: factorization or asymptotic equivalence for the stationary finite record; that
 181: gap is closed separately by Theorems~F and G.  The
 182: separate projection result is only the pointwise limit at the preselected
 183: population point \(z_0=1/2\), using the printed covariance certificate in
 184: \Cref{lem:z-half-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}.  No confidence set, test,
 185: critical value, coverage conclusion, or uniform projection claim is attached
 186: to it.
 187: Ordered labelled rates require external side information fixed independently
 188: of this record.  The paper does not claim
 189: simultaneous inversion over \(0<z<1\), nor identification of UDW, KMS,
 190: thermodynamic, response-profile, or ordered-rate quantities unless the
 191: particular result supplies the extra hypotheses and proof.
 192: 
 193: \subsection{Visible-record diagnostics for the model contract}\label{subsec:visible-record-model-diagnostics-main}
 194: 
 195: \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main} and
 196: \Cref{subsec:finite-record-report-scope-main} form a conditional contract, not a
 197: model-selection theorem.  The retained-record limits below are statements
 198: inside the killed-leakage sampled-counter D-MAP with known \(\Delta\tau\);
 199: they are not procedures that first validate that model from the same record and
 200: then authorize inference under it.  The physical-image test and the
 201: complete-visible-law test have only the size and power guarantees stated in
 202: \Cref{thm:uniform-joint-physical-image-test-main,thm:complete-visible-law-specification-main}.
 203: Auxiliary complete-gap renewal
 204: checks, inclusion-product residuals, and low-lag covariance residuals have no
 205: separate calibration theorem: they can falsify the standing interpretation,
 206: but they do not certify it or validate assumptions used by another result.
 207: 
 208: 
 209: \begin{lemma}[Latched sampled-counter derivation of the D-MAP kernels]\label{lem:classical-counter-kernel-construction-main}
 210: The kernels in \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main} are exactly the
 211: one-step kernels of the following discrete sampled-counter protocol.  At the
 212: start of a sampling interval of length \(\Delta\tau\), the hidden state is
 213: either \(R\) or \(D\).  From \(R\), an independent attempt clock with rate
 214: \(\Gamma\) either rings before the end of the interval, in which case the
 215: visible output is \(1\) and the counter is latched in \(D\) until the boundary,
 216: or it does not ring, in which case the visible output is \(0\) and the next
 217: state remains \(R\).
 218: From \(D\), an independent recovery clock with rate \(\kappa_{\mathrm r}\)
 219: either does not ring, giving output \(0\) and next state \(D\), or rings at
 220: time \(r\in(0,\Delta\tau)\).  Conditional on recovery at \(r\), the same
 221: attempt clock is run only during the remaining time \(\Delta\tau-r\): no
 222: attempt gives output \(0\) and next state \(R\), while an attempt gives output
 223: \(1\) and latches the counter in \(D\) until the boundary.  No post-click
 224: recovery or further within-bin evolution is permitted.  This protocol gives
 225: \[
 226: T_0(R,R)=p,\quad T_1(R,D)=1-p,\quad T_0(D,D)=s,
 227: \]
 228: \[
 229: T_0(D,R)=\int_0^{\Delta\tau}\kappa_{\mathrm r}e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}r}
 230: e^{-\Gamma(\Delta\tau-r)}\,dr=b,
 231: \quad
 232: T_1(D,D)=\int_0^{\Delta\tau}\kappa_{\mathrm r}e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}r}
 233: \bigl(1-e^{-\Gamma(\Delta\tau-r)}\bigr)\,dr=a,
 234: \]
 235: and the two killed entries \(T_1(R,R)=T_1(D,R)=0\).
 236: \end{lemma}
 237: 
 238: \begin{proof}
 239: The \(R\)-row is the survival and ringing decomposition of an exponential
 240: clock over one interval.  For the \(D\)-row, no recovery before
 241: \(\Delta\tau\) has probability \(s=e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau}\) and
 242: contributes to \(T_0(D,D)\).  If recovery occurs at \(r\), its density is
 243: \(\kappa_{\mathrm r}e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}r}\,dr\).  Survival of the attempt
 244: clock for the remaining time \(\Delta\tau-r\) gives the \(T_0(D,R)\) integral,
 245: and its complement gives the \(T_1(D,D)\) integral.  The latching rule never
 246: allows a marked transition landing in \(R\), which gives the two killed
 247: entries.  These mutually exclusive cases exhaust each row, since
 248: \(s+a+b=1\) and \(p+(1-p)=1\).
 249: \end{proof}
 250: 
 251: \begin{proposition}[Fragility under non-killed one-labelled leakage]\label{prop:model-fragility-boundary-reset-main}
 252: The killed-leakage convention in
 253: \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main} is not a removable presentation
 254: choice.  It is a structural hypothesis behind the renewal law, quotient
 255: inverse, and retained-record inference in Theorems~A, B, C, and E.  Let
 256: \((\widetilde T_0,\widetilde T_1)\) be any two-state labelled kernel with the
 257: same visible convention
 258: \[
 259: (\widetilde T_i)_{XY}
 260: =\PP(A_n=i,H_{n+1}=Y\mid H_n=X),\qquad X,Y\in\{R,D\},
 261: \]
 262: but suppose that either
 263: \[
 264: \widetilde T_1(R,R)>0
 265: \qquad\hbox{or}\qquad
 266: \widetilde T_1(D,R)>0 .
 267: \]
 268: Then a click no longer forces the next hidden state to be the deterministic
 269: state \(D\).  Consequently the click epochs are not regeneration epochs in
 270: general.  In particular, the Palm renewal product
 271: \[
 272: \PP(B\subset\Xi)=\rho\prod_j u_{i_{j+1}-i_j}
 273: \]
 274: for \(B=\{i_1<\cdots<i_m\}\) does not follow from the D-MAP structure alone;
 275: nor do the Palm gap formula
 276: \(g_k=e_D^\top T_0^kT_1\mathbf1\), the single-mode covariance identity
 277: \[
 278: u_2=\rho+(a-\rho)\lambda_{\rm hid},
 279: \]
 280: or the quotient recovery
 281: \[
 282: \lambda_{\rm hid}=(r_2-r_0^2)/(r_1-r_0^2),\qquad
 283: \Phi(r)=(p+s,ps).
 284: \]
 285: Therefore Theorems~A and B, and Theorems~C--E wherever they use the same
 286: renewal law, inverse, or covariance route, fail to be valid generic
 287: sampled-counter or generic D-MAP(2) statements unless additional hypotheses
 288: restore a deterministic post-click reset or supply a replacement regeneration
 289: theory.
 290: \end{proposition}
 291: 
 292: \begin{proof}
 293: The proofs of the lettered results use the following deterministic post-click fact:
 294: on every event \(\{A_n=1\}\), the next hidden state is \(H_{n+1}=D\).  In the
 295: kernel notation this is exactly
 296: \(T_1(R,R)=T_1(D,R)=0\).  It makes each observed click a reset to the same
 297: state \(D\), so the post-click future starts from the fixed vector \(e_D\),
 298: independently of the pre-click hidden state and of the earlier visible record.
 299: The inter-click zero runs are then i.i.d. under the Palm law, their tail is
 300: computed by iterating \(T_0\) from \(e_D\), and inclusion probabilities factor
 301: as the displayed renewal product.
 302: 
 303: If \(\widetilde T_1(R,R)>0\), a click from \(R\) can leave the next hidden
 304: state equal to \(R\).  If \(\widetilde T_1(D,R)>0\), a click from \(D\) can
 305: leave the next hidden state equal to \(R\).  Whenever either transition has
 306: positive probability, conditioning on \(A_n=1\) need not put \(H_{n+1}\) at
 307: the deterministic state \(D\); it produces a post-click distribution that can
 308: depend on the pre-click hidden state and on the stationary mixture at the
 309: click time.  The D-MAP property by itself only records labelled Markov
 310: transitions.  It does not turn this state-dependent post-click mixture into
 311: the fixed Palm restart required for a renewal record.
 312: 
 313: The continuous same-bin recovery comparator is a concrete instance: the paths
 314: ``click--recover'' from \(R\) and ``recover--click--recover'' from \(D\) give
 315: positive entries \(\widetilde T_1(R,R)\) and
 316: \(\widetilde T_1(D,R)\).  The Palm gap law is therefore no longer a consequence
 317: of the labelled kernel without extra assumptions.  The renewal product
 318: formulas and the covariance transfer lemma are downstream of that Palm renewal
 319: law, while the quotient inverse in Theorem~B explicitly divides the covariance
 320: identity \(r_2-r_0^2=\rho(a-\rho)\lambda_{\rm hid}\) by
 321: \(r_1-r_0^2=\rho(a-\rho)\).  Once the renewal identity is unavailable, the
 322: displayed inverse and the retained-record covariance estimator are no longer
 323: proved for the modified kernel.  This proves the stated logical dependence.
 324: \end{proof}
 325: 
 326: The main text below retains the five paper-level statements A--E for the
 327: constrained D-MAP(2) subfamily and adds the stationary collision Theorems~F
 328: and G.  Supporting lemmas, propositions, corollaries, certificate interfaces,
 329: and algorithms prove or apply these seven statements.  The killed-leakage dependency is
 330: explicit in \Cref{prop:model-fragility-boundary-reset-main}: if same-bin
 331: recovery after a click is retained in the one-labelled kernel, this theorem
 332: chain is not the applicable theorem chain.

+\subsection{Uniform score, stopping, plug-in, and two-point lemmas}
+\label{subsec:singular-uniform-lemmas-main}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform sampled-bin and sampled-tail derivatives]
+\label{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ \le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},\quad |a|\le3,
+\qquad
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ \le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},\quad |a|\le2.
+\tag{U1}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\).  In addition,
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Compress the colliding holding times into \(Y=X_1+X_2\).  Relative to
+Lebesgue measure on \((0,\infty)^{n-1}\), the complete holding-time density is
+\[
+ f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)
+ =(c^2-\delta)e^{-cy}\frac{\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)}{\sqrt\delta}
+ \prod_{j=3}^n\theta_j e^{-\theta_jx_j},
+\tag{U2}
+\]
+where the quotient at \(\delta=0\) is \(y\).  Write
+\(\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)/\sqrt\delta=y h(\delta y^2)\), where
+\(h(x)=\sinh(\sqrt x)/\sqrt x\) is positive and analytic on
+\([0,\infty)\).  On a sufficiently small common neighbourhood,
+\(c^2-\delta\) and every rate are bounded away from zero.  The derivatives
+through order three of \(\log h(x)\) are bounded on \([0,\infty)\): they are
+continuous at zero by the power series, and their elementary hyperbolic
+expressions are bounded as \(x\to\infty\).  Differentiating \(\log f_q\)
+therefore gives, uniformly on \(\mathcal Q^+\),
+\[
+ |\partial_q^a\log f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)|
+ \le C_a\{1+(y+x_3+\cdots+x_n)^{2|a|}\},
+ \qquad 1\le |a|\le3.
+\tag{U3}
+\]
+
+Put \(W=Y+X_3+\cdots+X_n\).  Differentiation under the integral in a
+sampling bin expresses every derivative of \(\log g_q(k)\) through order
+three as a finite universal polynomial in conditional expectations of the
+complete-data derivatives in \textup{(U3)}, conditional on
+\(k\Delta\tau<W\le(k+1)\Delta\tau\).  On this event every nonnegative
+holding time is at most \((k+1)\Delta\tau\), which proves the first bound in
+\textup{(U1)}.  This argument controls the ratio by the bin probability
+itself and hence does not infer a relative bound from an absolute derivative
+bound.
+
+For the tail ratios, each exponential density is log-concave, convolution
+preserves log-concavity, and integration over a half-line shows that the
+survival function of \(W\) is log-concave.  Thus \(W\) is IFR and its residual
+life satisfies
+\[
+ \PP_q(W-t>x\mid W>t)\le \PP_q(W>x),\qquad t,x\ge0.
+\tag{U4}
+\]
+All rates on \(\mathcal Q^+\) exceed a common \(\underline\theta>0\), so
+\(W\) is stochastically dominated by an
+Erlang\((n,\underline\theta)\) variable.  Consequently, for every fixed
+integer \(m\),
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}\EE_q(W^m\mid W>t)
+ \le C_m(1+t)^m.
+\tag{U5}
+\]
+The same conditional-score polynomial argument, now conditional on
+\(W>k\Delta\tau\), proves the second bound in \textup{(U1)}.  Finally,
+stochastic domination by the Erlang variable gives the common
+polynomial-exponential mass envelope.  The envelopes justify every
+differentiation under the integral and continuity at \(\delta=0\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform stopped renewal-score CLT and LLN]
+\label{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial age \(A_N\) and terminal residual \(R_N\), and put
+\(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in \(q\in\mathcal Q\), and also for
+triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),
+\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\tag{U6}
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous,
+\(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\tag{U7}
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\tag{U8}
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\(N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)\) uniformly.  These conclusions
+hold jointly and hence apply to the score, stopped Hessian, and third-order
+likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local triangular arrays.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The common exponential moment gives uniform bounds for every moment of
+\(D\), with \(0<\inf_q\mu_q\le\sup_q\mu_q<\infty\).  For the ordinary
+renewal count, compare the partial sums of \(D_j-\mu_q\) at
+\(\lfloor N/\mu_q\pm x\sqrt N\rfloor\).  Chebyshev's inequality and
+Kolmogorov's maximal inequality give a bound \(C/x^2\), uniformly in \(q\),
+for deviation of the count by more than \(x\sqrt N\).  The stationary delay
+changes this count only through the initial incomplete cycle, which is
+\(O_P(\log N)\) by the bound below.  This proves the first part of
+\textup{(U6)} without requiring independence between a reward and its cycle
+length.
+
+The equilibrium formula
+\(\PP_q(A_N\ge t)=\mu_q^{-1}\sum_{j\ge t}S_q(j)\), and its terminal analogue,
+have a common exponential-polynomial bound.  There are at most \(N\) complete
+gaps because \(D\ge1\).  A union bound for those gaps and the two endpoint
+variables therefore makes the probability that the maximum exceeds
+\(C_0\log N\) tend to zero uniformly for sufficiently large \(C_0\).  This
+proves the second part of \textup{(U6)}.
+
+For \(m_N=\lfloor N/\mu_q\rfloor\), the triangular-array Lindeberg theorem
+applied to the deterministic sum of \(b_q(G_j)\) gives the normal law in
+\textup{(U7)}.  The common polynomial envelope and exponential moment verify
+Lindeberg uniformly.  Replacing \(m_N\) by \(K_N\) changes the sum by at most
+the maximum of centred partial sums over \(O_P(\sqrt N)\) indices.
+Kolmogorov's inequality makes that difference \(o_P(\sqrt N)\) uniformly;
+this is the stopped-score, or Anscombe, step.  The same replacement in a
+law of large numbers is \(o_P(N)\), proving \textup{(U8)}.  The last assertion
+follows from \(K_N=O_P(N)\) and uniform integrability of the envelope.
+
+To verify the displayed uniformity rather than only pointwise convergence,
+take an arbitrary parameter sequence.  Compactness supplies a convergent
+subsequence; parameter continuity plus the common exponential envelope gives
+convergence of the means, covariance matrices, Lindeberg terms, and all LLN
+integrals along it.  The preceding inequalities have constants independent of
+the subsequence.  Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence with
+the asserted joint limits, which is the uniform subsequence criterion and
+also proves the triangular-array statement.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Efficient-score plug-in equicontinuity]
+\label{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\tag{U9}
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_{\eta}\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\tag{U10}
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Uniform nondegeneracy makes the projection coefficient in \textup{(U9)} twice
+continuously differentiable with polynomial score envelopes.  By construction,
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}\psi_\eta=0,
+ \qquad \EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U11}
+\]
+Differentiating the first identity, justified by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}, gives
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}(\partial_\eta\psi_\eta)
+ =-\EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U12}
+\]
+Thus the derivative of \(\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}\) is a normalized stopped sum
+of centred rewards and is \(O_P(1)\) uniformly by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}.  A second-order Taylor expansion
+over a ball of radius \(L/\sqrt N\) has first term \(O_P(N^{-1/2})\); its
+second term is bounded by
+\(N^{-1/2}O_P(N)O(N^{-1})=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).  This proves \textup{(U10)}.
+The stopped LLN applied to score outer products, followed by the same Taylor
+bound and continuity of matrix inversion on the uniformly positive-definite
+set, proves information consistency.  Contiguity transfers every null
+\(o_P(1)\) assertion to bounded local alternatives.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Two-point threshold-risk lower bound]
+\label{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}
+Fix a collision base \((\eta_0,0)\), hold \(\eta_0\) fixed, and compare
+\(P_{0,N}=P_{\eta_0,0}^{(N)}\) with
+\(P_{1,N}=P_{\eta_0,v_0/\sqrt N}^{(N)}\), where \(v_0>0\).  Let
+\(\mathcal R_{i,N}\) be their unordered rate multisets.  Then
+\[
+ d_{\rm m}(\mathcal R_{0,N},\mathcal R_{1,N})
+ =\sqrt{v_0}\,N^{-1/4},
+\tag{U13}
+\]
+and, for every \(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\),
+\[
+ \liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat{\mathcal R}_N}
+ \max_{i=0,1}P_{i,N}\!\left\{
+ N^{1/4}d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N,\mathcal R_{i,N})>a
+ \right\}
+ \ge \Phi_{\rm N}\!\left(
+ -\frac{v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}}2\right)>0.
+\tag{U14}
+\]
+Thus the lower conclusion is pointwise at a fixed base, uses two alternatives
+and threshold loss, and asserts optimality in rate rather than an exact
+minimax-risk theorem over a continuum of local parameters.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The two balls of radius \(aN^{-1/4}\) around the candidates are disjoint by
+\textup{(U13)}.  Assigning an estimate to its nearer candidate therefore
+turns simultaneous success of an estimator into correct testing of
+\(P_{0,N}\) against \(P_{1,N}\).  The LAN likelihood ratio under \(P_{0,N}\)
+converges to
+\[
+ \exp\{v_0Z-\tfrac12v_0^2I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)\},
+ \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)).
+\tag{U15}
+\]
+Its limit has mean one; mutual contiguity makes the likelihood ratios uniformly
+integrable, so their total-variation distances converge to that of the two
+Gaussian shifts separated by
+\(v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}\).  For any test, its maximum error is at
+least its equal-prior average error, whose limiting infimum is
+\(\Phi_{\rm N}\{-v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}/2\}\).  Taking a
+measurable estimator within \(o(1)\) of the infimum at each \(N\) proves
+\textup{(U14)}.  Strict positivity also follows directly from mutual
+contiguity, but \textup{(U14)} records the quantitative Gaussian bound.
+\end{proof}

+\subsection{Uniform score, stopping, plug-in, and two-point lemmas}
+\label{subsec:singular-uniform-lemmas-main}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform sampled-bin and sampled-tail derivatives]
+\label{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ \le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},\quad |a|\le3,
+\qquad
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ \le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},\quad |a|\le2.
+\tag{U1}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\).  In addition,
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Compress the colliding holding times into \(Y=X_1+X_2\).  Relative to
+Lebesgue measure on \((0,\infty)^{n-1}\), the complete holding-time density is
+\[
+ f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)
+ =(c^2-\delta)e^{-cy}\frac{\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)}{\sqrt\delta}
+ \prod_{j=3}^n\theta_j e^{-\theta_jx_j},
+\tag{U2}
+\]
+where the quotient at \(\delta=0\) is \(y\).  Write
+\(\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)/\sqrt\delta=y h(\delta y^2)\), where
+\(h(x)=\sinh(\sqrt x)/\sqrt x\) is positive and analytic on
+\([0,\infty)\).  On a sufficiently small common neighbourhood,
+\(c^2-\delta\) and every rate are bounded away from zero.  The derivatives
+through order three of \(\log h(x)\) are bounded on \([0,\infty)\): they are
+continuous at zero by the power series, and their elementary hyperbolic
+expressions are bounded as \(x\to\infty\).  Differentiating \(\log f_q\)
+therefore gives, uniformly on \(\mathcal Q^+\),
+\[
+ |\partial_q^a\log f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)|
+ \le C_a\{1+(y+x_3+\cdots+x_n)^{2|a|}\},
+ \qquad 1\le |a|\le3.
+\tag{U3}
+\]
+
+Put \(W=Y+X_3+\cdots+X_n\).  Differentiation under the integral in a
+sampling bin expresses every derivative of \(\log g_q(k)\) through order
+three as a finite universal polynomial in conditional expectations of the
+complete-data derivatives in \textup{(U3)}, conditional on
+\(k\Delta\tau<W\le(k+1)\Delta\tau\).  On this event every nonnegative
+holding time is at most \((k+1)\Delta\tau\), which proves the first bound in
+\textup{(U1)}.  This argument controls the ratio by the bin probability
+itself and hence does not infer a relative bound from an absolute derivative
+bound.
+
+For the tail ratios, each exponential density is log-concave, convolution
+preserves log-concavity, and integration over a half-line shows that the
+survival function of \(W\) is log-concave.  Thus \(W\) is IFR and its residual
+life satisfies
+\[
+ \PP_q(W-t>x\mid W>t)\le \PP_q(W>x),\qquad t,x\ge0.
+\tag{U4}
+\]
+All rates on \(\mathcal Q^+\) exceed a common \(\underline\theta>0\), so
+\(W\) is stochastically dominated by an
+Erlang\((n,\underline\theta)\) variable.  Consequently, for every fixed
+integer \(m\),
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}\EE_q(W^m\mid W>t)
+ \le C_m(1+t)^m.
+\tag{U5}
+\]
+The same conditional-score polynomial argument, now conditional on
+\(W>k\Delta\tau\), proves the second bound in \textup{(U1)}.  Finally,
+stochastic domination by the Erlang variable gives the common
+polynomial-exponential mass envelope.  The envelopes justify every
+differentiation under the integral and continuity at \(\delta=0\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform stopped renewal-score CLT and LLN]
+\label{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial age \(A_N\) and terminal residual \(R_N\), and put
+\(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in \(q\in\mathcal Q\), and also for
+triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),
+\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\tag{U6}
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous,
+\(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\tag{U7}
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\tag{U8}
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\(N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)\) uniformly.  These conclusions
+hold jointly and hence apply to the score, stopped Hessian, and third-order
+likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local triangular arrays.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The common exponential moment gives uniform bounds for every moment of
+\(D\), with \(0<\inf_q\mu_q\le\sup_q\mu_q<\infty\).  For the ordinary
+renewal count, compare the partial sums of \(D_j-\mu_q\) at
+\(\lfloor N/\mu_q\pm x\sqrt N\rfloor\).  Chebyshev's inequality and
+Kolmogorov's maximal inequality give a bound \(C/x^2\), uniformly in \(q\),
+for deviation of the count by more than \(x\sqrt N\).  The stationary delay
+changes this count only through the initial incomplete cycle, which is
+\(O_P(\log N)\) by the bound below.  This proves the first part of
+\textup{(U6)} without requiring independence between a reward and its cycle
+length.
+
+The equilibrium formula
+\(\PP_q(A_N\ge t)=\mu_q^{-1}\sum_{j\ge t}S_q(j)\), and its terminal analogue,
+have a common exponential-polynomial bound.  There are at most \(N\) complete
+gaps because \(D\ge1\).  A union bound for those gaps and the two endpoint
+variables therefore makes the probability that the maximum exceeds
+\(C_0\log N\) tend to zero uniformly for sufficiently large \(C_0\).  This
+proves the second part of \textup{(U6)}.
+
+For \(m_N=\lfloor N/\mu_q\rfloor\), the triangular-array Lindeberg theorem
+applied to the deterministic sum of \(b_q(G_j)\) gives the normal law in
+\textup{(U7)}.  The common polynomial envelope and exponential moment verify
+Lindeberg uniformly.  Replacing \(m_N\) by \(K_N\) changes the sum by at most
+the maximum of centred partial sums over \(O_P(\sqrt N)\) indices.
+Kolmogorov's inequality makes that difference \(o_P(\sqrt N)\) uniformly;
+this is the stopped-score, or Anscombe, step.  The same replacement in a
+law of large numbers is \(o_P(N)\), proving \textup{(U8)}.  The last assertion
+follows from \(K_N=O_P(N)\) and uniform integrability of the envelope.
+
+To verify the displayed uniformity rather than only pointwise convergence,
+take an arbitrary parameter sequence.  Compactness supplies a convergent
+subsequence; parameter continuity plus the common exponential envelope gives
+convergence of the means, covariance matrices, Lindeberg terms, and all LLN
+integrals along it.  The preceding inequalities have constants independent of
+the subsequence.  Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence with
+the asserted joint limits, which is the uniform subsequence criterion and
+also proves the triangular-array statement.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Efficient-score plug-in equicontinuity]
+\label{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\tag{U9}
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_{\eta}\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\tag{U10}
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Uniform nondegeneracy makes the projection coefficient in \textup{(U9)} twice
+continuously differentiable with polynomial score envelopes.  By construction,
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}\psi_\eta=0,
+ \qquad \EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U11}
+\]
+Differentiating the first identity, justified by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}, gives
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}(\partial_\eta\psi_\eta)
+ =-\EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U12}
+\]
+Thus the derivative of \(\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}\) is a normalized stopped sum
+of centred rewards and is \(O_P(1)\) uniformly by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}.  A second-order Taylor expansion
+over a ball of radius \(L/\sqrt N\) has first term \(O_P(N^{-1/2})\); its
+second term is bounded by
+\(N^{-1/2}O_P(N)O(N^{-1})=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).  This proves \textup{(U10)}.
+The stopped LLN applied to score outer products, followed by the same Taylor
+bound and continuity of matrix inversion on the uniformly positive-definite
+set, proves information consistency.  Contiguity transfers every null
+\(o_P(1)\) assertion to bounded local alternatives.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Two-point threshold-risk lower bound]
+\label{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}
+Fix a collision base \((\eta_0,0)\), hold \(\eta_0\) fixed, and compare
+\(P_{0,N}=P_{\eta_0,0}^{(N)}\) with
+\(P_{1,N}=P_{\eta_0,v_0/\sqrt N}^{(N)}\), where \(v_0>0\).  Let
+\(\mathcal R_{i,N}\) be their unordered rate multisets.  Then
+\[
+ d_{\rm m}(\mathcal R_{0,N},\mathcal R_{1,N})
+ =\sqrt{v_0}\,N^{-1/4},
+\tag{U13}
+\]
+and, for every \(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\),
+\[
+ \liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat{\mathcal R}_N}
+ \max_{i=0,1}P_{i,N}\!\left\{
+ N^{1/4}d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N,\mathcal R_{i,N})>a
+ \right\}
+ \ge \Phi_{\rm N}\!\left(
+ -\frac{v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}}2\right)>0.
+\tag{U14}
+\]
+Thus the lower conclusion is pointwise at a fixed base, uses two alternatives
+and threshold loss, and asserts optimality in rate rather than an exact
+minimax-risk theorem over a continuum of local parameters.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The two balls of radius \(aN^{-1/4}\) around the candidates are disjoint by
+\textup{(U13)}.  Assigning an estimate to its nearer candidate therefore
+turns simultaneous success of an estimator into correct testing of
+\(P_{0,N}\) against \(P_{1,N}\).  The LAN likelihood ratio under \(P_{0,N}\)
+converges to
+\[
+ \exp\{v_0Z-\tfrac12v_0^2I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)\},
+ \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)).
+\tag{U15}
+\]
+Its limit has mean one; mutual contiguity makes the likelihood ratios uniformly
+integrable, so their total-variation distances converge to that of the two
+Gaussian shifts separated by
+\(v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}\).  For any test, its maximum error is at
+least its equal-prior average error, whose limiting infimum is
+\(\Phi_{\rm N}\{-v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}/2\}\).  Taking a
+measurable estimator within \(o(1)\) of the infimum at each \(N\) proves
+\textup{(U14)}.  Strict positivity also follows directly from mutual
+contiguity, but \textup{(U14)} records the quantitative Gaussian bound.
+\end{proof}

   8: \begin{lemma}[Compact-uniform stationary renewal LAN]
   9: \label{lem:compact-uniform-stationary-renewal-lan-main}
  10: Let \(\mathcal Q_0\) be compact.  Suppose that, on a fixed one-sided
  11: neighbourhood of \(\mathcal Q_0\), the integer-valued Palm gap masses
  12: \(g_q(k)>0\) satisfy the following bounds for some \(r<1\):
  13: \[
  14:  \sup_q g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^m r^k,
  15:  \qquad
  16:  \sup_q|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|\le C_a(1+k)^{m_a},
  17:  \quad 1\le |a|\le3.
  18: \tag{SL1}
  19: \]
  20: Assume the same type of polynomial bound for the first two derivatives of
  21: \(\log S_q(k)\), where \(S_q(k)=\sum_{j\ge k}g_q(j)\), and put
  22: \(\mu_q=\sum_{k\ge0}S_q(k)\).  If
  23: \[
  24:  I(q)=\mu_q^{-1}\sum_{k\ge0}g_q(k)
  25:  \dot\ell_q(k)\dot\ell_q(k)^\top,
  26:  \qquad \dot\ell_q=\nabla_q\log g_q,
  27: \tag{SL2}
  28: \]
  29: is positive definite on \(\mathcal Q_0\), then the stationary binary renewal
  30: record is LAN, uniformly over \(q\in\mathcal Q_0\) and bounded admissible
  31: local vectors \(h\):
  32: \[
  33:  \log\frac{dP_{q+h/\sqrt N}^{(N)}}{dP_q^{(N)}}
  34:  =h^\top\Delta_{N,q}-\frac12h^\top I(q)h+o_{P_q}(1),
  35:  \qquad
  36:  \Delta_{N,q}\Rightarrow\mathcal N\{0,I(q)\}.
  37: \tag{SL3}
  38: \]
  39: The convergence of the central sequence and the remainder are compact-uniform.
  40: The conclusion remains valid when some coordinates of \(h\) are restricted
  41: to a closed convex cone.
  42: \end{lemma}
  43: 
  44: \begin{proof}
  45: Let the clicks in \([0,N-1]\) be
  46: \(0\le C_1<\cdots<C_J<N\), set
  47: \[
  48:  A=C_1,\qquad R=N-1-C_J,
  49:  \qquad G_j=C_{j+1}-C_j-1\quad(1\le j<J).
  50: \]
  51: For \(J\ge1\), stationary Palm inversion gives the exact record probability
  52: \[
  53:  P_q^{(N)}(A_0,\ldots,A_{N-1})
  54:  =\frac1{\mu_q}S_q(A)
  55:    \prod_{j=1}^{J-1}g_q(G_j)S_q(R).
  56: \tag{SL4}
  57: \]
  58: Indeed, \(S_q(A)/\mu_q\) is the equilibrium forward-recurrence mass of the
  59: first click, the displayed gaps are complete Palm cycles, and after the last
  60: click the absence of another click contributes \(S_q(R)\).  The no-click
  61: event is bounded by \(CN^{m+1}r^N\), uniformly in \(q\), by summing over the
  62: equilibrium cycle containing the whole window.
  63: 
  64: The common exponential envelope gives, uniformly in \(q\),
  65: \[
  66:  J/N\longrightarrow1/\mu_q,\qquad
  67:  J=N/\mu_q+O_{P_q}(\sqrt N),\qquad
  68:  \max\{A,R,G_1,\ldots,G_{J-1}\}=O_{P_q}(\log N).
  69: \tag{SL5}
  70: \]
  71: The first assertion is the uniform renewal law of large numbers; the second
  72: follows from the uniform finite-variance renewal CLT or maximal inequality;
  73: and the last follows by a union bound from \textup{(SL1)}.  The polynomial
  74: log-tail derivative bound and \textup{(SL5)} imply, for bounded \(h\),
  75: \[
  76:  \log\frac{\mu_q}{\mu_{q+h/\sqrt N}}
  77:  +\log\frac{S_{q+h/\sqrt N}(A)}{S_q(A)}
  78:  +\log\frac{S_{q+h/\sqrt N}(R)}{S_q(R)}=o_{P_q}(1)
  79: \tag{SL6}
  80: \]
  81: uniformly.  Thus the stationary endpoints do not alter the local experiment.
  82: 
  83: Taylor expansion of the complete-gap part of \textup{(SL4)} yields
  84: \[
  85:  \frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}h^\top\dot\ell_q(G_j)
  86:  +\frac1{2N}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}
  87:  h^\top\ddot\ell_q(G_j)h+o_{P_q}(1).
  88: \tag{SL7}
  89: \]
  90: The third-order remainder is uniform because \textup{(SL1)} supplies a
  91: common integrable polynomial envelope, so its expectation is \(O(N^{-1/2})\).
  92: Differentiating \(\sum_kg_q(k)=1\), justified by \textup{(SL1)}, gives
  93: \[
  94:  \EE_q\dot\ell_q(G)=0,\qquad
  95:  \EE_q\ddot\ell_q(G)=-\EE_q\{
  96:  \dot\ell_q(G)\dot\ell_q(G)^\top\}.
  97: \tag{SL8}
  98: \]
  99: The uniform law of large numbers, \textup{(SL5)}, and \textup{(SL8)} turn the
 100: second term in \textup{(SL7)} into \(-h^\top I(q)h/2+o_P(1)\).
 101: The stopped i.i.d. score CLT gives
 102: \[
 103:  \Delta_{N,q}:=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\dot\ell_q(G_j)
 104:  \Rightarrow\mathcal N\{0,I(q)\}.
 105: \tag{SL9}
 106: \]
 107: All assertions are uniform by the subsequence criterion: every sequence in
 108: the compact base set has a convergent subsequence, and the common exponential
 109: and polynomial envelopes give Lindeberg, uniform integrability, endpoint
 110: control, and the Taylor remainder along it.  Combining
 111: \textup{(SL4)}--\textup{(SL9)} proves \textup{(SL3)}.  Restricting local
 112: coordinates to a cone changes only the parameter set of the limit experiment.
 113: \end{proof}

 115: \begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:stationary-two-state-collision-main}]
 116: Let \(W=X_1+X_2\), where the two independent exponential holding times have
 117: rates \(c+d\) and \(c-d\).  Its Laplace transform and the transform of its
 118: continuous survival function are
 119: \[
 120:  \phi_{c,\delta}(s)
 121:  =\frac{c^2-\delta}{(s+c)^2-\delta},
 122:  \qquad
 123:  H_{c,\delta}(s)=\frac{1-\phi_{c,\delta}(s)}s.
 124: \tag{T21}
 125: \]
 126: Differentiation at \(\delta=0\) gives exactly \textup{(SC5)} and
 127: \[
 128:  \partial_cH_{c,0}(s)=-\frac{2c}{(s+c)^3}.
 129: \tag{T22}
 130: \]
 131: Inverse Laplace transformation and sampling at \(t=k\Delta\tau\) show that
 132: \(\partial_\delta S_{c,0}(k)\) has a nonzero cubic coefficient at
 133: \(e^{-c\Delta\tau k}\), whereas \(\partial_cS_{c,0}(k)\) has degree two.
 134: Taking first differences preserves linear independence.  Since every
 135: \(g_{c,0}(k)>0\), a linear combination of the two scores can vanish in
 136: \(L^2(g_{c,0})\) only if the corresponding linear combination of the mass
 137: derivatives, hence of the tail derivatives, vanishes at every \(k\).  The
 138: distinct polynomial degrees then force both coefficients to be zero.  This
 139: proves pointwise positive definiteness in \textup{(SC3)}.
 140: 
 141: On \([\varepsilon,M]\), partial-fraction inversion gives common bounds
 142: \[
 143:  |\partial_c^a\partial_\delta^b S_{c,\delta}(k)|
 144:  \le C_{a,b}(1+k)^{m_{a,b}}e^{-\varepsilon\Delta\tau k/2}
 145: \tag{T23}
 146: \]
 147: on a fixed neighbourhood with \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\).  The corresponding
 148: log-mass and log-tail derivatives have polynomial bounds; alternatively these
 149: bounds follow by differentiating the convolution law and conditioning on
 150: \(W>k\Delta\tau\) or on the sampled absorption bin.  Continuity of
 151: \(I_2(c)\), dominated by \textup{(T23)}, and compactness now give
 152: \textup{(SC6)}.  Applying
 153: \Cref{lem:compact-uniform-stationary-renewal-lan-main} with
 154: \(q=(c,\delta)\) proves \textup{(SC4)} and the half-plane limit.
 155: 
 156: For completeness, the efficient central sequence for the collision
 157: coordinate is
 158: \[
 159:  \Delta_{\delta\cdot c,N}
 160:  =\Delta_{\delta,N}-I_{\delta c}I_{cc}^{-1}\Delta_{c,N},
 161:  \qquad \Var(\Delta_{\delta\cdot c,N})\longrightarrow J_2(c).
 162: \tag{T24}
 163: \]
 164: Replacing \(c\) and the information entries by compact-uniform consistent
 165: null estimators changes the standardized statistic by \(o_P(1)\).  The third
 166: lemma gives mean \(v\sqrt{J_2(c)}\) under the local alternative.  The
 167: Neyman--Pearson lemma in the residual one-dimensional Gaussian shift gives
 168: \textup{(SC8)} and its envelope; the one-sided likelihood-ratio statistic is
 169: the square of the positive part of the same standardized score.  This is the
 170: standard Gaussian-cone conclusion
 171: \cite{Chernoff1954LikelihoodRatio,SelfLiang1987NonstandardLRT,
 172: vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}.
 173: 
 174: We next give an explicit rate-attaining estimator.  From the complete gaps in
 175: the stationary record define
 176: \[
 177:  \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
 178:  \qquad 0\le k\le3,
 179: \tag{T25}
 180: \]
 181: with an arbitrary fixed value on \(K_N=0\).  The endpoint deletion and the
 182: stopped i.i.d. CLT give
 183: \(\max_{k\le3}|\widehat S_k-S_k|=O_P(N^{-1/2})\) uniformly.  The order-two
 184: tail recurrence is
 185: \[
 186:  S_{k+2}-A S_{k+1}+B S_k=0,\qquad
 187:  A=z_1+z_2,\quad B=z_1z_2,\quad z_i=e^{-\theta_i\Delta\tau}.
 188: \tag{T26}
 189: \]
 190: Its leading Hankel matrix is nonsingular at the double pole by
 191: \Cref{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}; compactness makes
 192: the inverse uniform.  Solving the empirical version of \textup{(T26)} gives
 193: \((\widehat A,\widehat B)-(A,B)=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).
 194: 
 195: In a neighbourhood of \(A=2z,B=z^2\), the functions
 196: \[
 197:  c=-\frac1{2\Delta\tau}\log B,\qquad
 198:  \delta=\frac1{(\Delta\tau)^2}
 199:  \left[\operatorname{arcosh}\left(\frac{A}{2\sqrt B}\right)\right]^2
 200: \tag{T27}
 201: \]
 202: are real analytic after continuing the square of \(\operatorname{arcosh}\)
 203: through one.  Let \(\widetilde\delta_N\) be this analytic continuation and
 204: put \(\widehat\delta_N=(\widetilde\delta_N)^+\).  Then
 205: \[
 206:  \widehat c_N-c_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
 207:  \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2})
 208: \tag{T28}
 209: \]
 210: uniformly on bounded collision alternatives.  Because
 211: \(|\sqrt{x^+}-\sqrt{y}|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\) for \(y\ge0\), the pair
 212: \(\{\!\{\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\}\!\}\) satisfies
 213: \textup{(SC9)}.
 214: 
 215: Finally compare \(v=0\) and \(v=v_0\).  Their rate multisets are separated
 216: by \(\sqrt{v_0}N^{-1/4}\), while \textup{(SC4)} makes the two sequences of
 217: record laws mutually contiguous and gives a nondegenerate finite Gaussian
 218: likelihood ratio.  If an estimator made the two probabilities in
 219: \textup{(SC10)} tend to zero for an \(a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\), assigning the record
 220: to the closer of the two candidate multisets would consistently distinguish
 221: these contiguous experiments, a contradiction.  This proves
 222: \textup{(SC10)} and completes the two-state result.
 223: \end{proof}

+\subsection{Uniform score, stopping, plug-in, and two-point lemmas}
+\label{subsec:singular-uniform-lemmas-main}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform sampled-bin and sampled-tail derivatives]
+\label{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ \le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},\quad |a|\le3,
+\qquad
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ \le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},\quad |a|\le2.
+\tag{U1}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\).  In addition,
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Compress the colliding holding times into \(Y=X_1+X_2\).  Relative to
+Lebesgue measure on \((0,\infty)^{n-1}\), the complete holding-time density is
+\[
+ f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)
+ =(c^2-\delta)e^{-cy}\frac{\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)}{\sqrt\delta}
+ \prod_{j=3}^n\theta_j e^{-\theta_jx_j},
+\tag{U2}
+\]
+where the quotient at \(\delta=0\) is \(y\).  Write
+\(\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)/\sqrt\delta=y h(\delta y^2)\), where
+\(h(x)=\sinh(\sqrt x)/\sqrt x\) is positive and analytic on
+\([0,\infty)\).  On a sufficiently small common neighbourhood,
+\(c^2-\delta\) and every rate are bounded away from zero.  The derivatives
+through order three of \(\log h(x)\) are bounded on \([0,\infty)\): they are
+continuous at zero by the power series, and their elementary hyperbolic
+expressions are bounded as \(x\to\infty\).  Differentiating \(\log f_q\)
+therefore gives, uniformly on \(\mathcal Q^+\),
+\[
+ |\partial_q^a\log f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)|
+ \le C_a\{1+(y+x_3+\cdots+x_n)^{2|a|}\},
+ \qquad 1\le |a|\le3.
+\tag{U3}
+\]
+
+Put \(W=Y+X_3+\cdots+X_n\).  Differentiation under the integral in a
+sampling bin expresses every derivative of \(\log g_q(k)\) through order
+three as a finite universal polynomial in conditional expectations of the
+complete-data derivatives in \textup{(U3)}, conditional on
+\(k\Delta\tau<W\le(k+1)\Delta\tau\).  On this event every nonnegative
+holding time is at most \((k+1)\Delta\tau\), which proves the first bound in
+\textup{(U1)}.  This argument controls the ratio by the bin probability
+itself and hence does not infer a relative bound from an absolute derivative
+bound.
+
+For the tail ratios, each exponential density is log-concave, convolution
+preserves log-concavity, and integration over a half-line shows that the
+survival function of \(W\) is log-concave.  Thus \(W\) is IFR and its residual
+life satisfies
+\[
+ \PP_q(W-t>x\mid W>t)\le \PP_q(W>x),\qquad t,x\ge0.
+\tag{U4}
+\]
+All rates on \(\mathcal Q^+\) exceed a common \(\underline\theta>0\), so
+\(W\) is stochastically dominated by an
+Erlang\((n,\underline\theta)\) variable.  Consequently, for every fixed
+integer \(m\),
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}\EE_q(W^m\mid W>t)
+ \le C_m(1+t)^m.
+\tag{U5}
+\]
+The same conditional-score polynomial argument, now conditional on
+\(W>k\Delta\tau\), proves the second bound in \textup{(U1)}.  Finally,
+stochastic domination by the Erlang variable gives the common
+polynomial-exponential mass envelope.  The envelopes justify every
+differentiation under the integral and continuity at \(\delta=0\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform stopped renewal-score CLT and LLN]
+\label{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial age \(A_N\) and terminal residual \(R_N\), and put
+\(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in \(q\in\mathcal Q\), and also for
+triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),
+\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\tag{U6}
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous,
+\(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\tag{U7}
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\tag{U8}
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\(N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)\) uniformly.  These conclusions
+hold jointly and hence apply to the score, stopped Hessian, and third-order
+likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local triangular arrays.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The common exponential moment gives uniform bounds for every moment of
+\(D\), with \(0<\inf_q\mu_q\le\sup_q\mu_q<\infty\).  For the ordinary
+renewal count, compare the partial sums of \(D_j-\mu_q\) at
+\(\lfloor N/\mu_q\pm x\sqrt N\rfloor\).  Chebyshev's inequality and
+Kolmogorov's maximal inequality give a bound \(C/x^2\), uniformly in \(q\),
+for deviation of the count by more than \(x\sqrt N\).  The stationary delay
+changes this count only through the initial incomplete cycle, which is
+\(O_P(\log N)\) by the bound below.  This proves the first part of
+\textup{(U6)} without requiring independence between a reward and its cycle
+length.
+
+The equilibrium formula
+\(\PP_q(A_N\ge t)=\mu_q^{-1}\sum_{j\ge t}S_q(j)\), and its terminal analogue,
+have a common exponential-polynomial bound.  There are at most \(N\) complete
+gaps because \(D\ge1\).  A union bound for those gaps and the two endpoint
+variables therefore makes the probability that the maximum exceeds
+\(C_0\log N\) tend to zero uniformly for sufficiently large \(C_0\).  This
+proves the second part of \textup{(U6)}.
+
+For \(m_N=\lfloor N/\mu_q\rfloor\), the triangular-array Lindeberg theorem
+applied to the deterministic sum of \(b_q(G_j)\) gives the normal law in
+\textup{(U7)}.  The common polynomial envelope and exponential moment verify
+Lindeberg uniformly.  Replacing \(m_N\) by \(K_N\) changes the sum by at most
+the maximum of centred partial sums over \(O_P(\sqrt N)\) indices.
+Kolmogorov's inequality makes that difference \(o_P(\sqrt N)\) uniformly;
+this is the stopped-score, or Anscombe, step.  The same replacement in a
+law of large numbers is \(o_P(N)\), proving \textup{(U8)}.  The last assertion
+follows from \(K_N=O_P(N)\) and uniform integrability of the envelope.
+
+To verify the displayed uniformity rather than only pointwise convergence,
+take an arbitrary parameter sequence.  Compactness supplies a convergent
+subsequence; parameter continuity plus the common exponential envelope gives
+convergence of the means, covariance matrices, Lindeberg terms, and all LLN
+integrals along it.  The preceding inequalities have constants independent of
+the subsequence.  Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence with
+the asserted joint limits, which is the uniform subsequence criterion and
+also proves the triangular-array statement.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Efficient-score plug-in equicontinuity]
+\label{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\tag{U9}
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_{\eta}\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\tag{U10}
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Uniform nondegeneracy makes the projection coefficient in \textup{(U9)} twice
+continuously differentiable with polynomial score envelopes.  By construction,
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}\psi_\eta=0,
+ \qquad \EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U11}
+\]
+Differentiating the first identity, justified by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}, gives
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}(\partial_\eta\psi_\eta)
+ =-\EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U12}
+\]
+Thus the derivative of \(\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}\) is a normalized stopped sum
+of centred rewards and is \(O_P(1)\) uniformly by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}.  A second-order Taylor expansion
+over a ball of radius \(L/\sqrt N\) has first term \(O_P(N^{-1/2})\); its
+second term is bounded by
+\(N^{-1/2}O_P(N)O(N^{-1})=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).  This proves \textup{(U10)}.
+The stopped LLN applied to score outer products, followed by the same Taylor
+bound and continuity of matrix inversion on the uniformly positive-definite
+set, proves information consistency.  Contiguity transfers every null
+\(o_P(1)\) assertion to bounded local alternatives.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Two-point threshold-risk lower bound]
+\label{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}
+Fix a collision base \((\eta_0,0)\), hold \(\eta_0\) fixed, and compare
+\(P_{0,N}=P_{\eta_0,0}^{(N)}\) with
+\(P_{1,N}=P_{\eta_0,v_0/\sqrt N}^{(N)}\), where \(v_0>0\).  Let
+\(\mathcal R_{i,N}\) be their unordered rate multisets.  Then
+\[
+ d_{\rm m}(\mathcal R_{0,N},\mathcal R_{1,N})
+ =\sqrt{v_0}\,N^{-1/4},
+\tag{U13}
+\]
+and, for every \(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\),
+\[
+ \liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat{\mathcal R}_N}
+ \max_{i=0,1}P_{i,N}\!\left\{
+ N^{1/4}d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N,\mathcal R_{i,N})>a
+ \right\}
+ \ge \Phi_{\rm N}\!\left(
+ -\frac{v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}}2\right)>0.
+\tag{U14}
+\]
+Thus the lower conclusion is pointwise at a fixed base, uses two alternatives
+and threshold loss, and asserts optimality in rate rather than an exact
+minimax-risk theorem over a continuum of local parameters.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The two balls of radius \(aN^{-1/4}\) around the candidates are disjoint by
+\textup{(U13)}.  Assigning an estimate to its nearer candidate therefore
+turns simultaneous success of an estimator into correct testing of
+\(P_{0,N}\) against \(P_{1,N}\).  The LAN likelihood ratio under \(P_{0,N}\)
+converges to
+\[
+ \exp\{v_0Z-\tfrac12v_0^2I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)\},
+ \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)).
+\tag{U15}
+\]
+Its limit has mean one; mutual contiguity makes the likelihood ratios uniformly
+integrable, so their total-variation distances converge to that of the two
+Gaussian shifts separated by
+\(v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}\).  For any test, its maximum error is at
+least its equal-prior average error, whose limiting infimum is
+\(\Phi_{\rm N}\{-v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}/2\}\).  Taking a
+measurable estimator within \(o(1)\) of the infimum at each \(N\) proves
+\textup{(U14)}.  Strict positivity also follows directly from mutual
+contiguity, but \textup{(U14)} records the quantitative Gaussian bound.
+\end{proof}

+\subsection{Uniform score, stopping, plug-in, and two-point lemmas}
+\label{subsec:singular-uniform-lemmas-main}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform sampled-bin and sampled-tail derivatives]
+\label{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ \le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},\quad |a|\le3,
+\qquad
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ \le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},\quad |a|\le2.
+\tag{U1}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\).  In addition,
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Compress the colliding holding times into \(Y=X_1+X_2\).  Relative to
+Lebesgue measure on \((0,\infty)^{n-1}\), the complete holding-time density is
+\[
+ f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)
+ =(c^2-\delta)e^{-cy}\frac{\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)}{\sqrt\delta}
+ \prod_{j=3}^n\theta_j e^{-\theta_jx_j},
+\tag{U2}
+\]
+where the quotient at \(\delta=0\) is \(y\).  Write
+\(\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)/\sqrt\delta=y h(\delta y^2)\), where
+\(h(x)=\sinh(\sqrt x)/\sqrt x\) is positive and analytic on
+\([0,\infty)\).  On a sufficiently small common neighbourhood,
+\(c^2-\delta\) and every rate are bounded away from zero.  The derivatives
+through order three of \(\log h(x)\) are bounded on \([0,\infty)\): they are
+continuous at zero by the power series, and their elementary hyperbolic
+expressions are bounded as \(x\to\infty\).  Differentiating \(\log f_q\)
+therefore gives, uniformly on \(\mathcal Q^+\),
+\[
+ |\partial_q^a\log f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)|
+ \le C_a\{1+(y+x_3+\cdots+x_n)^{2|a|}\},
+ \qquad 1\le |a|\le3.
+\tag{U3}
+\]
+
+Put \(W=Y+X_3+\cdots+X_n\).  Differentiation under the integral in a
+sampling bin expresses every derivative of \(\log g_q(k)\) through order
+three as a finite universal polynomial in conditional expectations of the
+complete-data derivatives in \textup{(U3)}, conditional on
+\(k\Delta\tau<W\le(k+1)\Delta\tau\).  On this event every nonnegative
+holding time is at most \((k+1)\Delta\tau\), which proves the first bound in
+\textup{(U1)}.  This argument controls the ratio by the bin probability
+itself and hence does not infer a relative bound from an absolute derivative
+bound.
+
+For the tail ratios, each exponential density is log-concave, convolution
+preserves log-concavity, and integration over a half-line shows that the
+survival function of \(W\) is log-concave.  Thus \(W\) is IFR and its residual
+life satisfies
+\[
+ \PP_q(W-t>x\mid W>t)\le \PP_q(W>x),\qquad t,x\ge0.
+\tag{U4}
+\]
+All rates on \(\mathcal Q^+\) exceed a common \(\underline\theta>0\), so
+\(W\) is stochastically dominated by an
+Erlang\((n,\underline\theta)\) variable.  Consequently, for every fixed
+integer \(m\),
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}\EE_q(W^m\mid W>t)
+ \le C_m(1+t)^m.
+\tag{U5}
+\]
+The same conditional-score polynomial argument, now conditional on
+\(W>k\Delta\tau\), proves the second bound in \textup{(U1)}.  Finally,
+stochastic domination by the Erlang variable gives the common
+polynomial-exponential mass envelope.  The envelopes justify every
+differentiation under the integral and continuity at \(\delta=0\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform stopped renewal-score CLT and LLN]
+\label{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial age \(A_N\) and terminal residual \(R_N\), and put
+\(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in \(q\in\mathcal Q\), and also for
+triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),
+\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\tag{U6}
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous,
+\(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\tag{U7}
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\tag{U8}
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\(N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)\) uniformly.  These conclusions
+hold jointly and hence apply to the score, stopped Hessian, and third-order
+likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local triangular arrays.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The common exponential moment gives uniform bounds for every moment of
+\(D\), with \(0<\inf_q\mu_q\le\sup_q\mu_q<\infty\).  For the ordinary
+renewal count, compare the partial sums of \(D_j-\mu_q\) at
+\(\lfloor N/\mu_q\pm x\sqrt N\rfloor\).  Chebyshev's inequality and
+Kolmogorov's maximal inequality give a bound \(C/x^2\), uniformly in \(q\),
+for deviation of the count by more than \(x\sqrt N\).  The stationary delay
+changes this count only through the initial incomplete cycle, which is
+\(O_P(\log N)\) by the bound below.  This proves the first part of
+\textup{(U6)} without requiring independence between a reward and its cycle
+length.
+
+The equilibrium formula
+\(\PP_q(A_N\ge t)=\mu_q^{-1}\sum_{j\ge t}S_q(j)\), and its terminal analogue,
+have a common exponential-polynomial bound.  There are at most \(N\) complete
+gaps because \(D\ge1\).  A union bound for those gaps and the two endpoint
+variables therefore makes the probability that the maximum exceeds
+\(C_0\log N\) tend to zero uniformly for sufficiently large \(C_0\).  This
+proves the second part of \textup{(U6)}.
+
+For \(m_N=\lfloor N/\mu_q\rfloor\), the triangular-array Lindeberg theorem
+applied to the deterministic sum of \(b_q(G_j)\) gives the normal law in
+\textup{(U7)}.  The common polynomial envelope and exponential moment verify
+Lindeberg uniformly.  Replacing \(m_N\) by \(K_N\) changes the sum by at most
+the maximum of centred partial sums over \(O_P(\sqrt N)\) indices.
+Kolmogorov's inequality makes that difference \(o_P(\sqrt N)\) uniformly;
+this is the stopped-score, or Anscombe, step.  The same replacement in a
+law of large numbers is \(o_P(N)\), proving \textup{(U8)}.  The last assertion
+follows from \(K_N=O_P(N)\) and uniform integrability of the envelope.
+
+To verify the displayed uniformity rather than only pointwise convergence,
+take an arbitrary parameter sequence.  Compactness supplies a convergent
+subsequence; parameter continuity plus the common exponential envelope gives
+convergence of the means, covariance matrices, Lindeberg terms, and all LLN
+integrals along it.  The preceding inequalities have constants independent of
+the subsequence.  Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence with
+the asserted joint limits, which is the uniform subsequence criterion and
+also proves the triangular-array statement.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Efficient-score plug-in equicontinuity]
+\label{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\tag{U9}
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_{\eta}\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\tag{U10}
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Uniform nondegeneracy makes the projection coefficient in \textup{(U9)} twice
+continuously differentiable with polynomial score envelopes.  By construction,
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}\psi_\eta=0,
+ \qquad \EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U11}
+\]
+Differentiating the first identity, justified by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}, gives
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}(\partial_\eta\psi_\eta)
+ =-\EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U12}
+\]
+Thus the derivative of \(\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}\) is a normalized stopped sum
+of centred rewards and is \(O_P(1)\) uniformly by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}.  A second-order Taylor expansion
+over a ball of radius \(L/\sqrt N\) has first term \(O_P(N^{-1/2})\); its
+second term is bounded by
+\(N^{-1/2}O_P(N)O(N^{-1})=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).  This proves \textup{(U10)}.
+The stopped LLN applied to score outer products, followed by the same Taylor
+bound and continuity of matrix inversion on the uniformly positive-definite
+set, proves information consistency.  Contiguity transfers every null
+\(o_P(1)\) assertion to bounded local alternatives.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Two-point threshold-risk lower bound]
+\label{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}
+Fix a collision base \((\eta_0,0)\), hold \(\eta_0\) fixed, and compare
+\(P_{0,N}=P_{\eta_0,0}^{(N)}\) with
+\(P_{1,N}=P_{\eta_0,v_0/\sqrt N}^{(N)}\), where \(v_0>0\).  Let
+\(\mathcal R_{i,N}\) be their unordered rate multisets.  Then
+\[
+ d_{\rm m}(\mathcal R_{0,N},\mathcal R_{1,N})
+ =\sqrt{v_0}\,N^{-1/4},
+\tag{U13}
+\]
+and, for every \(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\),
+\[
+ \liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat{\mathcal R}_N}
+ \max_{i=0,1}P_{i,N}\!\left\{
+ N^{1/4}d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N,\mathcal R_{i,N})>a
+ \right\}
+ \ge \Phi_{\rm N}\!\left(
+ -\frac{v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}}2\right)>0.
+\tag{U14}
+\]
+Thus the lower conclusion is pointwise at a fixed base, uses two alternatives
+and threshold loss, and asserts optimality in rate rather than an exact
+minimax-risk theorem over a continuum of local parameters.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The two balls of radius \(aN^{-1/4}\) around the candidates are disjoint by
+\textup{(U13)}.  Assigning an estimate to its nearer candidate therefore
+turns simultaneous success of an estimator into correct testing of
+\(P_{0,N}\) against \(P_{1,N}\).  The LAN likelihood ratio under \(P_{0,N}\)
+converges to
+\[
+ \exp\{v_0Z-\tfrac12v_0^2I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)\},
+ \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)).
+\tag{U15}
+\]
+Its limit has mean one; mutual contiguity makes the likelihood ratios uniformly
+integrable, so their total-variation distances converge to that of the two
+Gaussian shifts separated by
+\(v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}\).  For any test, its maximum error is at
+least its equal-prior average error, whose limiting infimum is
+\(\Phi_{\rm N}\{-v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}/2\}\).  Taking a
+measurable estimator within \(o(1)\) of the infimum at each \(N\) proves
+\textup{(U14)}.  Strict positivity also follows directly from mutual
+contiguity, but \textup{(U14)} records the quantitative Gaussian bound.
+\end{proof}
