+\subsection{Uniform score, stopping, plug-in, and two-point lemmas}
+\label{subsec:singular-uniform-lemmas-main}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform sampled-bin and sampled-tail derivatives]
+\label{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{U1}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\).  In addition,
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Compress the colliding holding times into \(Y=X_1+X_2\).  Relative to
+Lebesgue measure on \((0,\infty)^{n-1}\), the complete holding-time density is
+\[
+ f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)
+ =(c^2-\delta)e^{-cy}\frac{\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)}{\sqrt\delta}
+ \prod_{j=3}^n\theta_j e^{-\theta_jx_j},
+\tag{U2}
+\]
+where the quotient at \(\delta=0\) is \(y\).  Write
+\(\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)/\sqrt\delta=y h(\delta y^2)\), where
+\(h(x)=\sinh(\sqrt x)/\sqrt x\) is positive and analytic on
+\([0,\infty)\).  On a sufficiently small common neighbourhood,
+\(c^2-\delta\) and every rate are bounded away from zero.  The derivatives
+through order three of \(\log h(x)\) are bounded on \([0,\infty)\): they are
+continuous at zero by the power series, and their elementary hyperbolic
+expressions are bounded as \(x\to\infty\).  Differentiating \(\log f_q\)
+therefore gives, uniformly on \(\mathcal Q^+\),
+\[
+ |\partial_q^a\log f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)|
+ \le C_a\{1+(y+x_3+\cdots+x_n)^{2|a|}\},
+ \qquad 1\le |a|\le3.
+\tag{U3}
+\]
+
+Put \(W=Y+X_3+\cdots+X_n\).  Differentiation under the integral in a
+sampling bin expresses every derivative of \(\log g_q(k)\) through order
+three as a finite universal polynomial in conditional expectations of the
+complete-data derivatives in \textup{(U3)}, conditional on
+\(k\Delta\tau<W\le(k+1)\Delta\tau\).  On this event every nonnegative
+holding time is at most \((k+1)\Delta\tau\), which proves the first bound in
+\textup{(U1)}.  This argument controls the ratio by the bin probability
+itself and hence does not infer a relative bound from an absolute derivative
+bound.
+
+For the tail ratios, each exponential density is log-concave, convolution
+preserves log-concavity, and integration over a half-line shows that the
+survival function of \(W\) is log-concave.  Thus \(W\) is IFR and its residual
+life satisfies
+\[
+ \PP_q(W-t>x\mid W>t)\le \PP_q(W>x),\qquad t,x\ge0.
+\tag{U4}
+\]
+All rates on \(\mathcal Q^+\) exceed a common \(\underline\theta>0\), so
+\(W\) is stochastically dominated by an
+Erlang\((n,\underline\theta)\) variable.  Consequently, for every fixed
+integer \(m\),
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}\EE_q(W^m\mid W>t)
+ \le C_m(1+t)^m.
+\tag{U5}
+\]
+The same conditional-score polynomial argument, now conditional on
+\(W>k\Delta\tau\), proves the second bound in \textup{(U1)}.  Finally,
+stochastic domination by the Erlang variable gives the common
+polynomial-exponential mass envelope.  The envelopes justify every
+differentiation under the integral and continuity at \(\delta=0\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform stopped renewal-score CLT and LLN]
+\label{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial age \(A_N\) and terminal residual \(R_N\), and put
+\(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in \(q\in\mathcal Q\), and also for
+triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),
+\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\tag{U6}
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous,
+\(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\tag{U7}
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\tag{U8}
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\(N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)\) uniformly.  These conclusions
+hold jointly and hence apply to the score, stopped Hessian, and third-order
+likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local triangular arrays.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The common exponential moment gives uniform bounds for every moment of
+\(D\), with \(0<\inf_q\mu_q\le\sup_q\mu_q<\infty\).  For the ordinary
+renewal count, compare the partial sums of \(D_j-\mu_q\) at
+\(\lfloor N/\mu_q\pm x\sqrt N\rfloor\).  Chebyshev's inequality and
+Kolmogorov's maximal inequality give a bound \(C/x^2\), uniformly in \(q\),
+for deviation of the count by more than \(x\sqrt N\).  The stationary delay
+changes this count only through the initial incomplete cycle, which is
+\(O_P(\log N)\) by the bound below.  This proves the first part of
+\textup{(U6)} without requiring independence between a reward and its cycle
+length.
+
+The equilibrium formula
+\(\PP_q(A_N\ge t)=\mu_q^{-1}\sum_{j\ge t}S_q(j)\), and its terminal analogue,
+have a common exponential-polynomial bound.  There are at most \(N\) complete
+gaps because \(D\ge1\).  A union bound for those gaps and the two endpoint
+variables therefore makes the probability that the maximum exceeds
+\(C_0\log N\) tend to zero uniformly for sufficiently large \(C_0\).  This
+proves the second part of \textup{(U6)}.
+
+For \(m_N=\lfloor N/\mu_q\rfloor\), the triangular-array Lindeberg theorem
+applied to the deterministic sum of \(b_q(G_j)\) gives the normal law in
+\textup{(U7)}.  The common polynomial envelope and exponential moment verify
+Lindeberg uniformly.  Replacing \(m_N\) by \(K_N\) changes the sum by at most
+the maximum of centred partial sums over \(O_P(\sqrt N)\) indices.
+Kolmogorov's inequality makes that difference \(o_P(\sqrt N)\) uniformly;
+this is the stopped-score, or Anscombe, step.  The same replacement in a
+law of large numbers is \(o_P(N)\), proving \textup{(U8)}.  The last assertion
+follows from \(K_N=O_P(N)\) and uniform integrability of the envelope.
+
+To verify the displayed uniformity rather than only pointwise convergence,
+take an arbitrary parameter sequence.  Compactness supplies a convergent
+subsequence; parameter continuity plus the common exponential envelope gives
+convergence of the means, covariance matrices, Lindeberg terms, and all LLN
+integrals along it.  The preceding inequalities have constants independent of
+the subsequence.  Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence with
+the asserted joint limits, which is the uniform subsequence criterion and
+also proves the triangular-array statement.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Efficient-score plug-in equicontinuity]
+\label{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\tag{U9}
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_{\eta}\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\tag{U10}
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Uniform nondegeneracy makes the projection coefficient in \textup{(U9)} twice
+continuously differentiable with polynomial score envelopes.  By construction,
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}\psi_\eta=0,
+ \qquad \EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U11}
+\]
+Differentiating the first identity, justified by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}, gives
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}(\partial_\eta\psi_\eta)
+ =-\EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U12}
+\]
+Thus the derivative of \(\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}\) is a normalized stopped sum
+of centred rewards and is \(O_P(1)\) uniformly by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}.  A second-order Taylor expansion
+over a ball of radius \(L/\sqrt N\) has first term \(O_P(N^{-1/2})\); its
+second term is bounded by
+\(N^{-1/2}O_P(N)O(N^{-1})=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).  This proves \textup{(U10)}.
+The stopped LLN applied to score outer products, followed by the same Taylor
+bound and continuity of matrix inversion on the uniformly positive-definite
+set, proves information consistency.  The normalization and the two
+stationary endpoint scores obey the same conclusion: their parameter
+increments are bounded by \(N^{-1/2}\) times a polynomial in
+\(\max(A_N,R_N)\), which is \(O_P(\log N)\) by \textup{(U6)}.  Thus they
+contribute \(o_P(1)\) uniformly to the plug-in difference.  Contiguity
+transfers every null \(o_P(1)\) assertion to bounded local alternatives.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Two-point threshold-risk lower bound]
+\label{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}
+Fix a collision base \((\eta_0,0)\), hold \(\eta_0\) fixed, and compare
+\(P_{0,N}=P_{\eta_0,0}^{(N)}\) with
+\(P_{1,N}=P_{\eta_0,v_0/\sqrt N}^{(N)}\), where \(v_0>0\).  Let
+\(\mathcal R_{i,N}\) be their unordered rate multisets.  Then
+\[
+ d_{\rm m}(\mathcal R_{0,N},\mathcal R_{1,N})
+ =\sqrt{v_0}\,N^{-1/4},
+\tag{U13}
+\]
+and, for every \(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\),
+\[
+ \liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat{\mathcal R}_N}
+ \max_{i=0,1}P_{i,N}\!\left\{
+ N^{1/4}d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N,\mathcal R_{i,N})>a
+ \right\}
+ \ge \Phi_{\rm N}\!\left(
+ -\frac{v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}}2\right)>0.
+\tag{U14}
+\]
+Thus the lower conclusion is pointwise at a fixed base, uses two alternatives
+and threshold loss, and asserts optimality in rate rather than an exact
+minimax-risk theorem over a continuum of local parameters.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The two balls of radius \(aN^{-1/4}\) around the candidates are disjoint by
+\textup{(U13)}.  Assigning an estimate to its nearer candidate therefore
+turns simultaneous success of an estimator into correct testing of
+\(P_{0,N}\) against \(P_{1,N}\).  The LAN likelihood ratio under \(P_{0,N}\)
+converges to
+\[
+ \exp\{v_0Z-\tfrac12v_0^2I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)\},
+ \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)).
+\tag{U15}
+\]
+Its limit has mean one; mutual contiguity makes the likelihood ratios uniformly
+integrable, so their total-variation distances converge to that of the two
+Gaussian shifts separated by
+\(v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}\).  For any test, its maximum error is at
+least its equal-prior average error, whose limiting infimum is
+\(\Phi_{\rm N}\{-v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}/2\}\).  Taking a
+measurable estimator within \(o(1)\) of the infimum at each \(N\) proves
+\textup{(U14)}.  Strict positivity also follows directly from mutual
+contiguity, but \textup{(U14)} records the quantitative Gaussian bound.
+\end{proof}

 158: \begin{lemma}[Efficient-score plug-in equicontinuity]
 159: \label{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}

 169: For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
 170: \[
 171:  \sup_{\eta}\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
 172:  |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
 173:  =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
 174: \tag{U10}
 175: \]
 176: The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
 177: empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
 178: in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
 179: \(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
 180: the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
 181: \end{lemma}
 182: 
 183: \begin{proof}
 184: Uniform nondegeneracy makes the projection coefficient in \textup{(U9)} twice
 185: continuously differentiable with polynomial score envelopes.  By construction,
 186: \[
 187:  \EE_{\eta,0}\psi_\eta=0,
 188:  \qquad \EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
 189: \tag{U11}
 190: \]
 191: Differentiating the first identity, justified by
 192: \Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}, gives
 193: \[
 194:  \EE_{\eta,0}(\partial_\eta\psi_\eta)
 195:  =-\EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
 196: \tag{U12}
 197: \]
 198: Thus the derivative of \(\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}\) is a normalized stopped sum
 199: of centred rewards and is \(O_P(1)\) uniformly by
 200: \Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}.  A second-order Taylor expansion
 201: over a ball of radius \(L/\sqrt N\) has first term \(O_P(N^{-1/2})\); its
 202: second term is bounded by
 203: \(N^{-1/2}O_P(N)O(N^{-1})=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).  This proves \textup{(U10)}.
 204: The stopped LLN applied to score outer products, followed by the same Taylor
 205: bound and continuity of matrix inversion on the uniformly positive-definite
 206: set, proves information consistency.  The normalization and the two
 207: stationary endpoint scores obey the same conclusion: their parameter
 208: increments are bounded by \(N^{-1/2}\) times a polynomial in
 209: \(\max(A_N,R_N)\), which is \(O_P(\log N)\) by \textup{(U6)}.  Thus they
 210: contribute \(o_P(1)\) uniformly to the plug-in difference.  Contiguity
 211: transfers every null \(o_P(1)\) assertion to bounded local alternatives.
 212: \end{proof}
 213: 
 214: \begin{lemma}[Two-point threshold-risk lower bound]
 215: \label{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}
 216: Fix a collision base \((\eta_0,0)\), hold \(\eta_0\) fixed, and compare
 217: \(P_{0,N}=P_{\eta_0,0}^{(N)}\) with
 218: \(P_{1,N}=P_{\eta_0,v_0/\sqrt N}^{(N)}\), where \(v_0>0\).  Let
 219: \(\mathcal R_{i,N}\) be their unordered rate multisets.  Then
 220: \[
 221:  d_{\rm m}(\mathcal R_{0,N},\mathcal R_{1,N})
 222:  =\sqrt{v_0}\,N^{-1/4},
 223: \tag{U13}
 224: \]
 225: and, for every \(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\),
 226: \[
 227:  \liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat{\mathcal R}_N}
 228:  \max_{i=0,1}P_{i,N}\!\left\{
 229:  N^{1/4}d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N,\mathcal R_{i,N})>a
 230:  \right\}
 231:  \ge \Phi_{\rm N}\!\left(
 232:  -\frac{v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}}2\right)>0.
 233: \tag{U14}
 234: \]
 235: Thus the lower conclusion is pointwise at a fixed base, uses two alternatives
 236: and threshold loss, and asserts optimality in rate rather than an exact
 237: minimax-risk theorem over a continuum of local parameters.
 238: \end{lemma}
 239: 
 240: \begin{proof}
 241: The two balls of radius \(aN^{-1/4}\) around the candidates are disjoint by
 242: \textup{(U13)}.  Assigning an estimate to its nearer candidate therefore
 243: turns simultaneous success of an estimator into correct testing of
 244: \(P_{0,N}\) against \(P_{1,N}\).  The LAN likelihood ratio under \(P_{0,N}\)
 245: converges to
 246: \[
 247:  \exp\{v_0Z-\tfrac12v_0^2I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)\},
 248:  \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)).
 249: \tag{U15}
 250: \]
 251: Its limit has mean one; mutual contiguity makes the likelihood ratios uniformly
 252: integrable, so their total-variation distances converge to that of the two
 253: Gaussian shifts separated by
 254: \(v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}\).  For any test, its maximum error is at
 255: least its equal-prior average error, whose limiting infimum is
 256: \(\Phi_{\rm N}\{-v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}/2\}\).  Taking a
 257: measurable estimator within \(o(1)\) of the infimum at each \(N\) proves
 258: \textup{(U14)}.  Strict positivity also follows directly from mutual
 259: contiguity, but \textup{(U14)} records the quantitative Gaussian bound.
 260: \end{proof}

   1: \section{Stationary collision experiments for sampled serial phase-type renewals}
   2: \label{sec:stationary-serial-collision-main}

   4: This section changes the inferential object from a deterministic product of
   5: complete Palm gaps to the stationary binary record itself.  We first close
   6: that gap for the present two-state sampled counter and then treat one isolated
   7: double collision in an arbitrary fixed serial order.  Throughout this section
   8: the sampling interval \(\Delta\tau>0\) is known.
   9: 
  10: For two finite multisets \(A=\{\!\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}\!\}\) and
  11: \(B=\{\!\{b_1,\ldots,b_n\}\!\}\), write
  12: \[
  13:  d_{\rm m}(A,B)=\min_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n}
  14:        \max_{1\le i\le n}|a_i-b_{\pi(i)}|
  15: \tag{SC1}

  19: \begin{paperthm}[Stationary two-state exchange experiment and sharp recovery]
  20: \label{thm:stationary-two-state-collision-main}
  21: Fix \(0<\varepsilon<M<\infty\).  In the sampled-counter model of
  22: \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, use the quotient coordinates
  23: \[
  24:  c=\frac{\Gamma+\kappa_{\mathrm r}}2,
  25:  \qquad d=\frac{\Gamma-\kappa_{\mathrm r}}2,
  26:  \qquad \delta=d^2\ge0.
  27: \tag{SC2}
  28: \]
  29: Let \(P_{c,\delta}^{(N)}\) be the law of the stationary binary record
  30: \((A_0,\ldots,A_{N-1})\), and let \(g_{c,\delta}\), \(S_{c,\delta}\), and
  31: \(\mu_{c,\delta}=\sum_{k\ge0}S_{c,\delta}(k)\) denote its Palm gap mass,
  32: tail, and mean cycle length.  At \(\delta=0\), set
  33: \[
  34:  \dot\ell_c(k)=\partial_c\log g_{c,0}(k),\qquad
  35:  \dot\ell_\delta(k)=\partial_\delta\log g_{c,\delta}(k)|_{\delta=0},
  36: \]
  37: and define the calendar information
  38: \[
  39:  I_2(c)=\frac1{\mu_{c,0}}
  40:  \sum_{k\ge0}g_{c,0}(k)
  41:  \begin{pmatrix}\dot\ell_c(k)\\ \dot\ell_\delta(k)\end{pmatrix}
  42:  \begin{pmatrix}\dot\ell_c(k)&\dot\ell_\delta(k)\end{pmatrix}.
  43: \tag{SC3}
  44: \]
  45: Then the following conclusions hold uniformly for \(c\in[\varepsilon,M]\).
  46: 
  47: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.6em]
  48: \item If \(u\in\RR\) and \(v\in[0,\infty)\) range over bounded sets, then
  49: \[
  50:  \log\frac{dP_{c+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N}^{(N)}}
  51:                {dP_{c,0}^{(N)}}
  52:  =\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}\Delta_{N,c}
  53:  -\frac12\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}
  54:  I_2(c)\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}+o_{P_{c,0}}(1),
  55: \tag{SC4}
  56: \]
  57: where the remainder is uniform in \((c,u,v)\) and
  58: \(\Delta_{N,c}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_2\{0,I_2(c)\}\) uniformly in bounded
  59: Lipschitz distance.  Thus the stationary-record experiments converge to the
  60: Gaussian shift on the half-plane \(\RR\times[0,\infty)\).
  61: 
  62: \item The continuous survival transform has a double pole at the collision,
  63: whereas its collision derivative has an exact fourth-order pole:
  64: \[
  65:  \mathcal L\{\overline F_{c,\delta}\}(s)
  66:  =\frac1s\left\{1-
  67:  \frac{c^2-\delta}{(s+c)^2-\delta}\right\},
  68: \quad
  69:  \partial_\delta\mathcal L\{\overline F_{c,\delta}\}(s)|_0
  70:  =\frac{s+2c}{(s+c)^4}.
  71: \tag{SC5}
  72: \]
  73: The centre derivative is \(-2c/(s+c)^3\).  Consequently the sampled
  74: collision derivative contains a nonzero
  75: \(k^3e^{-c\Delta\tau k}\) term, while the centre derivative has degree at
  76: most two at that exponential base.  Hence
  77: \[
  78:  \inf_{c\in[\varepsilon,M]}\lambda_{\min}\{I_2(c)\}>0.
  79: \tag{SC6}
  80: \]
  81: 
  82: \item Partition \(I_2\) according to \((c,\delta)\) and put
  83: \[
  84:  J_2(c)=I_{\delta\delta}
  85:  -I_{\delta c}I_{cc}^{-1}I_{c\delta}>0.
  86: \tag{SC7}
  87: \]
  88: For testing \(H_0:\delta=0\) against \(H_1:\delta>0\), the residualized
  89: score test, equivalently the local likelihood-ratio test, is asymptotically
  90: level \(\alpha\) uniformly in \(c\).  At
  91: \((c_N,\delta_N)=(c+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N)\) its limiting power is
  92: \[
  93:  1-\Phi_{\rm N}\{z_{1-\alpha}-v\sqrt{J_2(c)}\}.
  94: \tag{SC8}
  95: \]
  96: This is the Gaussian half-plane power envelope among tests with uniform local
  97: asymptotic level \(\alpha\).
  98: 
  99: \item There is an estimator \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N\) of the unordered rate
 100: pair such that, uniformly for bounded \((u,v)\),
 101: \[
 102:  d_{\rm m}\left(
 103:  \widehat{\mathcal R}_N,
 104:  \{\!\{c+u/\sqrt N+\sqrt{v/\sqrt N},
 105:           c+u/\sqrt N-\sqrt{v/\sqrt N}\}\!\}\right)
 106:  =O_P(N^{-1/4}).
 107: \tag{SC9}
 108: \]
 109: The estimated centre is root-\(N\), and the estimator first obtains a
 110: root-\(N\) estimate of \(\delta\) and projects it onto \([0,\infty)\).
 111: Conversely, for every fixed \(c\in(\varepsilon,M)\), \(v_0>0\), and
 112: \(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\),
 113: \[
 114:  \liminf_{N\to\infty}\ \inf_{\widehat{\mathcal R}_N}
 115:  \max_{v\in\{0,v_0\}}
 116:  P_{c,v/\sqrt N}^{(N)}\!\left\{
 117:  N^{1/4}d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N,
 118:  \{\!\{c+\sqrt{v/\sqrt N},c-\sqrt{v/\sqrt N}\}\!\})>a
 119:  \right\}>0.
 120: \tag{SC10}
 121: \]
 122: Thus \(N^{-1/4}\) is uniformly attainable and pointwise locally
 123: minimax-optimal in rate, as witnessed by this fixed-base two-point threshold
 124: lower bound.  No exact minimax-risk constant is asserted.  The sign of \(d\)
 125: is not identifiable.
 126: \end{enumerate}
 127: \end{paperthm}

 150: \begin{paperthm}[Stationary double-pole experiment for sampled generalized-Erlang renewals]

 100: \begin{lemma}[Measurable finite-atlas quotient estimator from sampled tails]
 101: \label{lem:serial-collision-recurrence-estimator-main}
 102: Under the restrictions of \Cref{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main}, there
 103: are measurable estimators \((\widehat\eta_N,\widehat\delta_N)\), with the
 104: noncollision entries of \(\widehat\eta_N\) canonically ordered and
 105: \(\widehat\delta_N\ge0\), such that for every bounded set of local parameters
 106: \[
 107:  \widehat\eta_N-\eta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),
 108:  \qquad
 109:  \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2})
 110: \tag{P6}
 111: \]
 112: uniformly over the compact stratum.  The induced rate multiset satisfies
 113: \textup{(SC19)}.
 114: \end{lemma}

 116: \begin{proof}
 117: Delete the initial and terminal incomplete cycles and write the observed
 118: complete gaps as \(G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\).  Define
 119: \[
 120:  \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
 121:  \qquad 0\le k\le2n-1,
 122: \tag{P7}
 123: \]
 124: with arbitrary fixed values on \(K_N=0\).  Apply
 125: \Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main} to the finite vector of indicator
 126: rewards.  Its stopped CLT and count bound imply
 127: \[
 128:  \max_{0\le k\le2n-1}|\widehat S_k-S_k|=O_P(N^{-1/2})
 129: \tag{P8}
 130: \]
 131: uniformly over the stratum and bounded local alternatives.
 132: 
 133: Write the monic recurrence polynomial as
 134: \[
 135:  \chi(x)=x^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_0
 136:  =\prod_{i=1}^n(x-z_i),\qquad z_i=e^{-\theta_i\Delta\tau}.
 137: \tag{P9}
 138: \]
 139: The equations
 140: \[
 141:  S_{k+n}+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}a_jS_{k+j}=0,\qquad0\le k<n,
 142: \tag{P10}
 143: \]
 144: have coefficient matrix \((S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n}\).  It is nonsingular even
 145: at collisions by
 146: \Cref{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}.  Its determinant
 147: has a positive minimum in absolute value on the compact stratum; the same is
 148: true on a sufficiently small common neighbourhood.  Solving the empirical
 149: version of \textup{(P10)} and using \textup{(P8)} therefore gives
 150: \[
 151:  \max_j|\widehat a_j-a_j|=O_P(N^{-1/2})
 152: \tag{P11}
 153: \]
 154: uniformly.
 155: 
 156: We now distinguish the cluster from the noncollision roots.  In sampled-root
 157: coordinates, the separation in rates gives the common distance
 158: \(\rho_0=\Delta\tau e^{-M\Delta\tau}c_0>0\).  At each base polynomial choose
 159: one circle enclosing its double root and \(n-2\) disjoint circles enclosing
 160: its simple roots, all with radii below \(\rho_0/4\).  On a coefficient
 161: neighbourhood \(U\), the argument principle keeps the root counts equal to
 162: two and one, respectively.  For a simple-root circle the contour power sum
 163: \[
 164:  z_j(a)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\gamma_j}
 165:  z\,\frac{\chi_a'(z)}{\chi_a(z)}\,dz
 166: \tag{P12}
 167: \]
 168: is analytic.  On the double-root circle the corresponding first and second
 169: power sums \(p_1,p_2\) are analytic, and
 170: \[
 171:  A=p_1,\qquad B=(p_1^2-p_2)/2
 172: \tag{P13}
 173: \]
 174: are the elementary symmetric functions of the two-root cluster.  These
 175: formulas remain analytic when the two roots split; no individual label is
 176: assigned inside the cluster.
 177: 
 178: The compact collision stratum in coefficient space is covered by finitely
 179: many such neighbourhoods \(U_1,\ldots,U_L\).  Shrink them to open sets
 180: \(V_\ell\) whose closures lie in \(U_\ell\) and still cover the stratum.
 181: Define the chart index to be the least \(\ell\) with
 182: \(\widehat a\in V_\ell\).  Membership in a finite collection of open sets is
 183: Borel measurable.  In every chart, order the real simple roots by their
 184: rates \(-\log z/\Delta\tau\); on overlaps the ordered simple-root vector and
 185: the cluster power sums agree, so the selection cannot change the estimand.
 186: The finite maximum of the chart derivatives is bounded.
 187: 
 188: By \textup{(P11)}, for every deterministic sequence \(C_N\to\infty\),
 189: \[
 190:  \sup_qP_q\{\|\widehat a-a(q)\|>C_N/\sqrt N\}\longrightarrow0.
 191: \tag{P14}
 192: \]
 193: The finite shrunken cover has a positive Lebesgue-number margin in coefficient
 194: space.  Coefficients on bounded local alternatives are \(O(N^{-1/2})\) from
 195: the base stratum and hence lie within half that margin for all sufficiently
 196: large \(N\).  Thus \textup{(P14)} implies that the probability of no valid
 197: chart tends to zero uniformly.  On that exceptional event use a fixed ordered
 198: value.
 199: Otherwise the analytic maps, \textup{(P11)}, and the finite derivative bound
 200: give root-\(N\) errors for every ordered simple root and for \(A,B\).  The
 201: separated rates are \(-\log z_j/\Delta\tau\), while the double-cluster
 202: quotient coordinates are the analytic functions in \textup{(T27)}.  Project
 203: the continued \(\widetilde\delta_N\) onto \([0,\infty)\); projection is
 204: nonexpansive.  This proves \textup{(P6)} and the claimed measurability.
 205: 
 206: Finally form the estimated double pair
 207: \(\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\) and the estimated separated
 208: rates.  The square-root inequality used after \textup{(T28)} gives
 209: \(O_P(N^{-1/4})\) for the colliding pair, while all other components are
 210: root-\(N\).  The separation \(c_0\) fixes the optimal matching with
 211: probability tending to one uniformly, proving \textup{(SC19)}.
 212: \end{proof}
 213: 
 214: \begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main}]
 215: The serial killed-reset construction makes the visible record a stationary
 216: renewal record whose Palm cycle is the sampled absorption bin of
 217: \(W=X_1+\cdots+X_n\).  In particular,
 218: \[
 219:  S_{\eta,\delta}(k)=P_{\eta,\delta}
 220:  \{W>k\Delta\tau\},\qquad
 221:  g_{\eta,\delta}(k)=S_{\eta,\delta}(k)-S_{\eta,\delta}(k+1).
 222: \tag{G1}
 223: \]
 224: \Cref{lem:sampled-double-pole-nondegeneracy-main} verifies every analytic,
 225: tail, and information hypothesis of
 226: \Cref{lem:compact-uniform-stationary-renewal-lan-main}.  Applying that lemma
 227: with \(q=(\eta,\delta)\) proves \textup{(SC15)}--\textup{(SC16)}.  Notice
 228: that the proof uses the exact stationary factorization \textup{(SL4)}: its
 229: random number of complete gaps supplies the factor \(1/\mu\) in
 230: \textup{(SC14)}, and its two survival factors and \(1/\mu\) are
 231: \(o_P(1)\) in the local log likelihood.  Thus no deterministic-product
 232: equivalence is being assumed.
 233: 
 234: For testing, define the efficient collision central sequence
 235: \[
 236:  \Delta_{\delta\cdot\eta,N}
 237:  =\Delta_{\delta,N}
 238:  -I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}\Delta_{\eta,N}.
 239: \tag{G2}
 240: \]
 241: It has null variance \(J_n\), which is strictly positive by the Schur
 242: complement of \textup{(SC16)}.  Under
 243: \((\eta_N,\delta_N)=(\eta_0+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N)\), Le Cam's third lemma gives
 244: mean \(vJ_n\); the nuisance shift cancels in \textup{(G2)}.  A null fit from
 245: \Cref{lem:serial-collision-recurrence-estimator-main}, followed by evaluation
 246: of the scores and information at \((\widehat\eta_N,0)\), changes
 247: \(\Delta_{\delta\cdot\eta,N}/\sqrt{J_n}\) by \(o_P(1)\) uniformly.  Rejecting
 248: above \(z_{1-\alpha}\) therefore gives \textup{(SC18)}.  The Gaussian
 249: Neyman--Pearson bound after residualizing the nuisance proves the asserted
 250: power envelope; maximizing the local quadratic likelihood over
 251: \(v\ge0\) yields the same rejection rule.
 252: 
 253: The plug-in assertion in the preceding paragraph is precisely
 254: \Cref{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}: efficient orthogonality centres the
 255: parameter derivative of the score, while the stopped LLN controls the
 256: estimated information.  It does not rely on the recurrence fit satisfying a
 257: likelihood score equation.
 258: 
 259: The finite-atlas estimator lemma proves the uniform upper rate
 260: \textup{(SC19)}, including the root-\(N\) rate for the centre, collision
 261: square, and canonically ordered noncollision rates.  For the lower bound, fix
 262: a base point and hold \(\eta=\eta_0\) fixed while comparing \(v=0\) with
 263: \(v=v_0>0\).  \Cref{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main} gives their exact
 264: \(\sqrt{v_0}N^{-1/4}\) matching distance and the positive lower bound
 265: \[
 266:  \Phi_{\rm N}\!\left\{
 267:  -\frac{v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}}2\right\}
 268: \tag{G3}
 269: \]
 270: for the two-point threshold risk.  Together with \textup{(SC19)}, this proves
 271: uniform attainability and pointwise local minimax optimality in rate, with no
 272: claim of an exact minimax constant over a continuum of alternatives.  This
 273: completes the theorem.
 274: \end{proof}

+two and one, respectively.  For a simple-root circle the contour power sum
+\[
+ z_j(a)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\gamma_j}
+ z\,\frac{\chi_a'(z)}{\chi_a(z)}\,dz
+\tag{P12}
+\]
+is analytic.  On the double-root circle the corresponding first and second
+power sums \(p_1,p_2\) are analytic, and
+\[
+ A=p_1,\qquad B=(p_1^2-p_2)/2
+\tag{P13}
+\]
+are the elementary symmetric functions of the two-root cluster.  These
+formulas remain analytic when the two roots split; no individual label is
+assigned inside the cluster.
+
+The compact collision stratum in coefficient space is covered by finitely
+many such neighbourhoods \(U_1,\ldots,U_L\).  Shrink them to open sets
+\(V_\ell\) whose closures lie in \(U_\ell\) and still cover the stratum.
+Define the chart index to be the least \(\ell\) with
+\(\widehat a\in V_\ell\).  Membership in a finite collection of open sets is
+Borel measurable.  In every chart, order the real simple roots by their
+rates \(-\log z/\Delta\tau\); on overlaps the ordered simple-root vector and
+the cluster power sums agree, so the selection cannot change the estimand.
+The finite maximum of the chart derivatives is bounded.
+
+By \textup{(P11)}, for every deterministic sequence \(C_N\to\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_qP_q\{\|\widehat a-a(q)\|>C_N/\sqrt N\}\longrightarrow0.
+\tag{P14}
+\]
+The finite shrunken cover has a positive Lebesgue-number margin in coefficient
+space.  Coefficients on bounded local alternatives are \(O(N^{-1/2})\) from
+the base stratum and hence lie within half that margin for all sufficiently
+large \(N\).  Thus \textup{(P14)} implies that the probability of no valid
+chart tends to zero uniformly.  On that exceptional event use a fixed ordered
+value.
+Otherwise the analytic maps, \textup{(P11)}, and the finite derivative bound
+give root-\(N\) errors for every ordered simple root and for \(A,B\).  The
+separated rates are \(-\log z_j/\Delta\tau\), while the double-cluster
+quotient coordinates are the analytic functions in \textup{(T27)}.  Project
+the continued \(\widetilde\delta_N\) onto \([0,\infty)\); projection is
+nonexpansive.  This proves \textup{(P6)} and the claimed measurability.

+\subsection{Uniform score, stopping, plug-in, and two-point lemmas}
+\label{subsec:singular-uniform-lemmas-main}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform sampled-bin and sampled-tail derivatives]
+\label{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{U1}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\).  In addition,
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Compress the colliding holding times into \(Y=X_1+X_2\).  Relative to
+Lebesgue measure on \((0,\infty)^{n-1}\), the complete holding-time density is
+\[
+ f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)
+ =(c^2-\delta)e^{-cy}\frac{\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)}{\sqrt\delta}
+ \prod_{j=3}^n\theta_j e^{-\theta_jx_j},
+\tag{U2}
+\]
+where the quotient at \(\delta=0\) is \(y\).  Write
+\(\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)/\sqrt\delta=y h(\delta y^2)\), where
+\(h(x)=\sinh(\sqrt x)/\sqrt x\) is positive and analytic on
+\([0,\infty)\).  On a sufficiently small common neighbourhood,
+\(c^2-\delta\) and every rate are bounded away from zero.  The derivatives
+through order three of \(\log h(x)\) are bounded on \([0,\infty)\): they are
+continuous at zero by the power series, and their elementary hyperbolic
+expressions are bounded as \(x\to\infty\).  Differentiating \(\log f_q\)
+therefore gives, uniformly on \(\mathcal Q^+\),
+\[
+ |\partial_q^a\log f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)|
+ \le C_a\{1+(y+x_3+\cdots+x_n)^{2|a|}\},
+ \qquad 1\le |a|\le3.
+\tag{U3}
+\]
+
+Put \(W=Y+X_3+\cdots+X_n\).  Differentiation under the integral in a
+sampling bin expresses every derivative of \(\log g_q(k)\) through order
+three as a finite universal polynomial in conditional expectations of the
+complete-data derivatives in \textup{(U3)}, conditional on
+\(k\Delta\tau<W\le(k+1)\Delta\tau\).  On this event every nonnegative
+holding time is at most \((k+1)\Delta\tau\), which proves the first bound in
+\textup{(U1)}.  This argument controls the ratio by the bin probability
+itself and hence does not infer a relative bound from an absolute derivative
+bound.
+
+For the tail ratios, each exponential density is log-concave, convolution
+preserves log-concavity, and integration over a half-line shows that the
+survival function of \(W\) is log-concave.  Thus \(W\) is IFR and its residual
+life satisfies
+\[
+ \PP_q(W-t>x\mid W>t)\le \PP_q(W>x),\qquad t,x\ge0.
+\tag{U4}
+\]
+All rates on \(\mathcal Q^+\) exceed a common \(\underline\theta>0\), so
+\(W\) is stochastically dominated by an
+Erlang\((n,\underline\theta)\) variable.  Consequently, for every fixed
+integer \(m\),
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}\EE_q(W^m\mid W>t)
+ \le C_m(1+t)^m.
+\tag{U5}
+\]
+The same conditional-score polynomial argument, now conditional on
+\(W>k\Delta\tau\), proves the second bound in \textup{(U1)}.  Finally,
+stochastic domination by the Erlang variable gives the common
+polynomial-exponential mass envelope.  The envelopes justify every
+differentiation under the integral and continuity at \(\delta=0\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform stopped renewal-score CLT and LLN]
+\label{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial age \(A_N\) and terminal residual \(R_N\), and put
+\(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in \(q\in\mathcal Q\), and also for
+triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),
+\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\tag{U6}
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous,
+\(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\tag{U7}
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\tag{U8}
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\(N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)\) uniformly.  These conclusions
+hold jointly and hence apply to the score, stopped Hessian, and third-order
+likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local triangular arrays.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The common exponential moment gives uniform bounds for every moment of
+\(D\), with \(0<\inf_q\mu_q\le\sup_q\mu_q<\infty\).  For the ordinary
+renewal count, compare the partial sums of \(D_j-\mu_q\) at
+\(\lfloor N/\mu_q\pm x\sqrt N\rfloor\).  Chebyshev's inequality and
+Kolmogorov's maximal inequality give a bound \(C/x^2\), uniformly in \(q\),
+for deviation of the count by more than \(x\sqrt N\).  The stationary delay
+changes this count only through the initial incomplete cycle, which is
+\(O_P(\log N)\) by the bound below.  This proves the first part of
+\textup{(U6)} without requiring independence between a reward and its cycle
+length.
+
+The equilibrium formula
+\(\PP_q(A_N\ge t)=\mu_q^{-1}\sum_{j\ge t}S_q(j)\), and its terminal analogue,
+have a common exponential-polynomial bound.  There are at most \(N\) complete
+gaps because \(D\ge1\).  A union bound for those gaps and the two endpoint
+variables therefore makes the probability that the maximum exceeds
+\(C_0\log N\) tend to zero uniformly for sufficiently large \(C_0\).  This
+proves the second part of \textup{(U6)}.
+
+For \(m_N=\lfloor N/\mu_q\rfloor\), the triangular-array Lindeberg theorem
+applied to the deterministic sum of \(b_q(G_j)\) gives the normal law in
+\textup{(U7)}.  The common polynomial envelope and exponential moment verify
+Lindeberg uniformly.  Replacing \(m_N\) by \(K_N\) changes the sum by at most
+the maximum of centred partial sums over \(O_P(\sqrt N)\) indices.
+Kolmogorov's inequality makes that difference \(o_P(\sqrt N)\) uniformly;
+this is the stopped-score, or Anscombe, step.  The same replacement in a
+law of large numbers is \(o_P(N)\), proving \textup{(U8)}.  The last assertion
+follows from \(K_N=O_P(N)\) and uniform integrability of the envelope.
+
+To verify the displayed uniformity rather than only pointwise convergence,
+take an arbitrary parameter sequence.  Compactness supplies a convergent
+subsequence; parameter continuity plus the common exponential envelope gives
+convergence of the means, covariance matrices, Lindeberg terms, and all LLN
+integrals along it.  The preceding inequalities have constants independent of
+the subsequence.  Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence with
+the asserted joint limits, which is the uniform subsequence criterion and
+also proves the triangular-array statement.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Efficient-score plug-in equicontinuity]
+\label{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\tag{U9}
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_{\eta}\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\tag{U10}
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Uniform nondegeneracy makes the projection coefficient in \textup{(U9)} twice
+continuously differentiable with polynomial score envelopes.  By construction,
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}\psi_\eta=0,
+ \qquad \EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U11}
+\]
+Differentiating the first identity, justified by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}, gives
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}(\partial_\eta\psi_\eta)
+ =-\EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U12}
+\]
+Thus the derivative of \(\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}\) is a normalized stopped sum
+of centred rewards and is \(O_P(1)\) uniformly by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}.  A second-order Taylor expansion
+over a ball of radius \(L/\sqrt N\) has first term \(O_P(N^{-1/2})\); its
+second term is bounded by
+\(N^{-1/2}O_P(N)O(N^{-1})=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).  This proves \textup{(U10)}.
+The stopped LLN applied to score outer products, followed by the same Taylor
+bound and continuity of matrix inversion on the uniformly positive-definite
+set, proves information consistency.  The normalization and the two
+stationary endpoint scores obey the same conclusion: their parameter
+increments are bounded by \(N^{-1/2}\) times a polynomial in
+\(\max(A_N,R_N)\), which is \(O_P(\log N)\) by \textup{(U6)}.  Thus they
+contribute \(o_P(1)\) uniformly to the plug-in difference.  Contiguity
+transfers every null \(o_P(1)\) assertion to bounded local alternatives.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Two-point threshold-risk lower bound]
+\label{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}
+Fix a collision base \((\eta_0,0)\), hold \(\eta_0\) fixed, and compare
+\(P_{0,N}=P_{\eta_0,0}^{(N)}\) with
+\(P_{1,N}=P_{\eta_0,v_0/\sqrt N}^{(N)}\), where \(v_0>0\).  Let
+\(\mathcal R_{i,N}\) be their unordered rate multisets.  Then
+\[
+ d_{\rm m}(\mathcal R_{0,N},\mathcal R_{1,N})
+ =\sqrt{v_0}\,N^{-1/4},
+\tag{U13}
+\]
+and, for every \(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\),
+\[
+ \liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat{\mathcal R}_N}
+ \max_{i=0,1}P_{i,N}\!\left\{
+ N^{1/4}d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N,\mathcal R_{i,N})>a
+ \right\}
+ \ge \Phi_{\rm N}\!\left(
+ -\frac{v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}}2\right)>0.
+\tag{U14}
+\]
+Thus the lower conclusion is pointwise at a fixed base, uses two alternatives
+and threshold loss, and asserts optimality in rate rather than an exact
+minimax-risk theorem over a continuum of local parameters.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The two balls of radius \(aN^{-1/4}\) around the candidates are disjoint by
+\textup{(U13)}.  Assigning an estimate to its nearer candidate therefore
+turns simultaneous success of an estimator into correct testing of
+\(P_{0,N}\) against \(P_{1,N}\).  The LAN likelihood ratio under \(P_{0,N}\)
+converges to
+\[
+ \exp\{v_0Z-\tfrac12v_0^2I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)\},
+ \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)).
+\tag{U15}
+\]
+Its limit has mean one; mutual contiguity makes the likelihood ratios uniformly
+integrable, so their total-variation distances converge to that of the two
+Gaussian shifts separated by
+\(v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}\).  For any test, its maximum error is at
+least its equal-prior average error, whose limiting infimum is
+\(\Phi_{\rm N}\{-v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}/2\}\).  Taking a
+measurable estimator within \(o(1)\) of the infimum at each \(N\) proves
+\textup{(U14)}.  Strict positivity also follows directly from mutual
+contiguity, but \textup{(U14)} records the quantitative Gaussian bound.
+\end{proof}

   1: \subsection{Stationary likelihood reduction and the two-state proof}
   2: \label{subsec:stationary-renewal-lan-proof-main}
   3: 
   4: We use the following renewal lemma with a finite-dimensional parameter
   5: \(q\).  Its uniform formulation is included because replacing a deterministic
   6: number of Palm gaps by the stationary record is essential here.
   7: 
   8: \begin{lemma}[Compact-uniform stationary renewal LAN]
   9: \label{lem:compact-uniform-stationary-renewal-lan-main}
  10: Let \(\mathcal Q_0\) be compact.  Suppose that, on a fixed one-sided
  11: neighbourhood of \(\mathcal Q_0\), the integer-valued Palm gap masses
  12: \(g_q(k)>0\) satisfy the following bounds for some \(r<1\):
  13: \[
  14:  \sup_q g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^m r^k,
  15:  \qquad
  16:  \sup_q|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|\le C_a(1+k)^{m_a},
  17:  \quad 1\le |a|\le3.
  18: \tag{SL1}
  19: \]
  20: Assume the same type of polynomial bound for the first two derivatives of
  21: \(\log S_q(k)\), where \(S_q(k)=\sum_{j\ge k}g_q(j)\), and put
  22: \(\mu_q=\sum_{k\ge0}S_q(k)\).  If
  23: \[
  24:  I(q)=\mu_q^{-1}\sum_{k\ge0}g_q(k)
  25:  \dot\ell_q(k)\dot\ell_q(k)^\top,
  26:  \qquad \dot\ell_q=\nabla_q\log g_q,
  27: \tag{SL2}
  28: \]
  29: is positive definite on \(\mathcal Q_0\), then the stationary binary renewal
  30: record is LAN, uniformly over \(q\in\mathcal Q_0\) and bounded admissible
  31: local vectors \(h\):
  32: \[
  33:  \log\frac{dP_{q+h/\sqrt N}^{(N)}}{dP_q^{(N)}}
  34:  =h^\top\Delta_{N,q}-\frac12h^\top I(q)h+o_{P_q}(1),
  35:  \qquad
  36:  \Delta_{N,q}\Rightarrow\mathcal N\{0,I(q)\}.
  37: \tag{SL3}
  38: \]
  39: The convergence of the central sequence and the remainder are compact-uniform.
  40: The conclusion remains valid when some coordinates of \(h\) are restricted
  41: to a closed convex cone.
  42: \end{lemma}
  43: 
  44: \begin{proof}
  45: Let the clicks in \([0,N-1]\) be
  46: \(0\le C_1<\cdots<C_J<N\), set
  47: \[
  48:  A=C_1,\qquad R=N-1-C_J,
  49:  \qquad G_j=C_{j+1}-C_j-1\quad(1\le j<J).
  50: \]
  51: For \(J\ge1\), stationary Palm inversion gives the exact record probability
  52: \[
  53:  P_q^{(N)}(A_0,\ldots,A_{N-1})
  54:  =\frac1{\mu_q}S_q(A)
  55:    \prod_{j=1}^{J-1}g_q(G_j)S_q(R).
  56: \tag{SL4}
  57: \]
  58: Indeed, \(S_q(A)/\mu_q\) is the equilibrium forward-recurrence mass of the
  59: first click, the displayed gaps are complete Palm cycles, and after the last
  60: click the absence of another click contributes \(S_q(R)\).  The no-click
  61: event is bounded by \(CN^{m+1}r^N\), uniformly in \(q\), by summing over the
  62: equilibrium cycle containing the whole window.
  63: 
  64: \Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}, applied with
  65: \(K_N=J-1\), gives uniformly in \(q\),
  66: \[
  67:  J/N\longrightarrow1/\mu_q,\qquad
  68:  J=N/\mu_q+O_{P_q}(\sqrt N),\qquad
  69:  \max\{A,R,G_1,\ldots,G_{J-1}\}=O_{P_q}(\log N).
  70: \tag{SL5}
  71: \]
  72: including for every bounded local triangular array.  Taylor's theorem for
  73: \(\log\mu_q\), the polynomial log-tail derivative bound, and
  74: \textup{(SL5)} imply, for bounded \(h\),
  75: \[
  76:  \log\frac{\mu_q}{\mu_{q+h/\sqrt N}}
  77:  +\log\frac{S_{q+h/\sqrt N}(A)}{S_q(A)}
  78:  +\log\frac{S_{q+h/\sqrt N}(R)}{S_q(R)}=o_{P_q}(1)
  79: \tag{SL6}
  80: \]
  81: uniformly.  Thus the stationary endpoints do not alter the local experiment.
  82: 
  83: Taylor expansion of the complete-gap part of \textup{(SL4)} yields
  84: \[
  85:  \frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}h^\top\dot\ell_q(G_j)
  86:  +\frac1{2N}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}
  87:  h^\top\ddot\ell_q(G_j)h+o_{P_q}(1).
  88: \tag{SL7}
  89: \]
  90: The third-order remainder is uniform by the last assertion of
  91: \Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}: after the \(N^{-3/2}\)
  92: Taylor factor, the stopped sum of the common polynomial envelope is
  93: \(o_P(1)\).
  94: Differentiating \(\sum_kg_q(k)=1\), justified by \textup{(SL1)}, gives
  95: \[
  96:  \EE_q\dot\ell_q(G)=0,\qquad
  97:  \EE_q\ddot\ell_q(G)=-\EE_q\{
  98:  \dot\ell_q(G)\dot\ell_q(G)^\top\}.
  99: \tag{SL8}
 100: \]
 101: The stopped Hessian LLN \textup{(U8)} and \textup{(SL8)} turn the second
 102: term in \textup{(SL7)} into \(-h^\top I(q)h/2+o_P(1)\).  The bounded-
 103: Lipschitz stopped-score CLT \textup{(U7)} gives
 104: \[
 105:  \Delta_{N,q}:=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\dot\ell_q(G_j)
 106:  \Rightarrow\mathcal N\{0,I(q)\}.
 107: \tag{SL9}
 108: \]
 109: The cited stopped-renewal lemma proves these assertions jointly and uniformly,
 110: including under the local triangular arrays.  Combining
 111: \textup{(SL4)}--\textup{(SL9)} proves \textup{(SL3)}.  Restricting local
 112: coordinates to a cone changes only the parameter set of the limit experiment.
 113: \end{proof}
 114: 
 115: \begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:stationary-two-state-collision-main}]
 116: Let \(W=X_1+X_2\), where the two independent exponential holding times have
 117: rates \(c+d\) and \(c-d\).  Its Laplace transform and the transform of its
 118: continuous survival function are
 119: \[
 120:  \phi_{c,\delta}(s)
 121:  =\frac{c^2-\delta}{(s+c)^2-\delta},
 122:  \qquad
 123:  H_{c,\delta}(s)=\frac{1-\phi_{c,\delta}(s)}s.
 124: \tag{T21}
 125: \]
 126: Differentiation at \(\delta=0\) gives exactly \textup{(SC5)} and
 127: \[
 128:  \partial_cH_{c,0}(s)=-\frac{2c}{(s+c)^3}.
 129: \tag{T22}
 130: \]
 131: Inverse Laplace transformation and sampling at \(t=k\Delta\tau\) show that
 132: \(\partial_\delta S_{c,0}(k)\) has a nonzero cubic coefficient at
 133: \(e^{-c\Delta\tau k}\), whereas \(\partial_cS_{c,0}(k)\) has degree two.
 134: Taking first differences preserves linear independence.  Since every
 135: \(g_{c,0}(k)>0\), a linear combination of the two scores can vanish in
 136: \(L^2(g_{c,0})\) only if the corresponding linear combination of the mass
 137: derivatives, hence of the tail derivatives, vanishes at every \(k\).  The
 138: distinct polynomial degrees then force both coefficients to be zero.  This
 139: proves pointwise positive definiteness in \textup{(SC3)}.
 140: 
 141: On \([\varepsilon,M]\), partial-fraction inversion gives common absolute
 142: bounds
 143: \[
 144:  |\partial_c^a\partial_\delta^b S_{c,\delta}(k)|
 145:  \le C_{a,b}(1+k)^{m_{a,b}}e^{-\varepsilon\Delta\tau k/2}
 146: \tag{T23}
 147: \]
 148: on a fixed neighbourhood with \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\).  The relative log-mass
 149: and log-tail bounds do not follow from \textup{(T23)} alone; they follow from
 150: the conditional complete-data argument in
 151: \Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}, specialized to \(n=2\).
 152: Continuity of \(I_2(c)\), dominated by that lemma, and compactness now give
 153: \textup{(SC6)}.  Applying
 154: \Cref{lem:compact-uniform-stationary-renewal-lan-main} with
 155: \(q=(c,\delta)\) proves \textup{(SC4)} and the half-plane limit.
 156: 
 157: For completeness, the efficient central sequence for the collision
 158: coordinate is
 159: \[
 160:  \Delta_{\delta\cdot c,N}
 161:  =\Delta_{\delta,N}-I_{\delta c}I_{cc}^{-1}\Delta_{c,N},
 162:  \qquad \Var(\Delta_{\delta\cdot c,N})\longrightarrow J_2(c).
 163: \tag{T24}
 164: \]
 165: Replacing \(c\) by the root-\(N\) null recurrence fit and the information
 166: entries by their empirical versions changes the standardized statistic by
 167: \(o_P(1)\), by \Cref{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}.  Le Cam's third lemma
 168: gives mean \(v\sqrt{J_2(c)}\) under the local alternative.  The
 169: Neyman--Pearson lemma in the residual one-dimensional Gaussian shift gives
 170: \textup{(SC8)} and its envelope; the one-sided likelihood-ratio statistic is
 171: the square of the positive part of the same standardized score.  This is the
 172: standard Gaussian-cone conclusion
 173: \cite{Chernoff1954LikelihoodRatio,SelfLiang1987NonstandardLRT,
 174: vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}.
 175: 
 176: We next give an explicit rate-attaining estimator.  From the complete gaps in
 177: the stationary record define
 178: \[
 179:  \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
 180:  \qquad 0\le k\le3,
 181: \tag{T25}
 182: \]
 183: with an arbitrary fixed value on \(K_N=0\).  The endpoint deletion and the
 184: stopped i.i.d. CLT give
 185: \(\max_{k\le3}|\widehat S_k-S_k|=O_P(N^{-1/2})\) uniformly.  The order-two
 186: tail recurrence is
 187: \[
 188:  S_{k+2}-A S_{k+1}+B S_k=0,\qquad
 189:  A=z_1+z_2,\quad B=z_1z_2,\quad z_i=e^{-\theta_i\Delta\tau}.
 190: \tag{T26}
 191: \]
 192: Its leading Hankel matrix is nonsingular at the double pole by
 193: \Cref{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}; compactness makes
 194: the inverse uniform.  Solving the empirical version of \textup{(T26)} gives
 195: \((\widehat A,\widehat B)-(A,B)=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).
 196: 
 197: In a neighbourhood of \(A=2z,B=z^2\), the functions
 198: \[
 199:  c=-\frac1{2\Delta\tau}\log B,\qquad
 200:  \delta=\frac1{(\Delta\tau)^2}
 201:  \left[\operatorname{arcosh}\left(\frac{A}{2\sqrt B}\right)\right]^2
 202: \tag{T27}
 203: \]
 204: are real analytic after continuing the square of \(\operatorname{arcosh}\)
 205: through one.  Let \(\widetilde\delta_N\) be this analytic continuation and
 206: put \(\widehat\delta_N=(\widetilde\delta_N)^+\).  Then
 207: \[
 208:  \widehat c_N-c_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
 209:  \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2})
 210: \tag{T28}
 211: \]
 212: uniformly on bounded collision alternatives.  Because
 213: \(|\sqrt{x^+}-\sqrt{y}|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\) for \(y\ge0\), the pair
 214: \(\{\!\{\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\}\!\}\) satisfies
 215: \textup{(SC9)}.
 216: 
 217: Finally apply \Cref{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main} with \(n=2\).  It gives
 218: both the disjoint-ball reduction and the strictly positive Gaussian testing
 219: lower bound, and therefore proves \textup{(SC10)}.  This completes the
 220: two-state result.
 221: \end{proof}

 203: \subsection{Sampled-counter interpretation}
 204: 
 205: Continuous dead-time and exponential-recovery detector models motivate the
 206: two-state parametrization
 207: \cite{YuFessler2000,SarbaziSafariHaas2018LongDeadTime,
 208: KrauseWalenta2025SPADRecovery}.  They do not provide the theorem object here:
 209: continuous within-bin recovery after a click can give a marked transition into
 210: the ready state, whereas the present D-MAP latches every click in the dead
 211: state until the boundary.  The sampled counter is therefore an interpretation
 212: of the constrained kernel, not an independently analysed physical system.

   1: \begin{abstract}
   2: We determine the stationary-record limit experiment when two rates collide in
   3: a sampled generalized-Erlang, equivalently serial discrete phase-type, renewal
   4: process.  For fixed serial order, one isolated double collision, compact
   5: positive rate sets, uniformly separated remaining rates, and known sampling
   6: interval, the smooth identifiable coordinate is the squared half-separation
   7: \(\delta=\{(\theta_1-\theta_2)/2\}^2\).  The exact stationary likelihood,
   8: including equilibrium age and residual-life factors and random renewal
   9: stopping, is uniformly locally asymptotically normal in the regular nuisance
  10: coordinates and \(\delta\) at rate \(N^{-1/2}\).  The collision derivative has
  11: an exact fourth-order pole and a nonzero
  12: \(k^3e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau k}\) sampled component; this proves uniform
  13: information nondegeneracy against all nuisance derivatives.  The limit is a
  14: Gaussian shift on a half-space, its residualized score test attains the
  15: one-sided local power envelope.  The unordered rate multiset has a uniformly
  16: attainable \(N^{-1/4}\) rate and a matching pointwise fixed-base two-point
  17: threshold lower rate; no exact minimax-risk constant is claimed.  The centre
  18: and all canonically ordered noncolliding rates remain root-\(N\).  We first
  19: prove the complete stationary experiment
  20: for the present two-state sampled counter and then prove the fixed-order serial
  21: theorem.
  22: 
  23: The underlying killed-reset D-MAP makes the visible process renewal but does
  24: not make its hidden representation identifiable.  We retain the explicit
  25: two-state Palm law, weak-equivalence cone intersection, and fixed-setting
  26: record tools as population and inferential complements.  Three visible
  27: inclusion probabilities give a rational inverse to \((p+s,ps)\).  This
  28: three-inclusion formula is presented as a candidate original result pending
  29: complete reduction against canonical DMAP2 coordinates; it identifies the
  30: unordered pair, not a labelled realization.  The pure serial population
  31: inverse remains a finite-coordinate sampled-tail specialization of the
  32: generalized-Erlang and Coxian representation theory of He--Zhang.  Supplementary
  33: calculations are separated from the stationary collision theorem.
  34: \end{abstract}
  35: 
  36: \noindent\textbf{Keywords:} generalized-Erlang distribution, serial phase
  37: type, singular LAN, minimax rate, stationary renewal record, double pole,
  38: constrained D-MAP
  39: 
  40: \section{Introduction}
  41: 
  42: The main question is statistical rather than representational: what is the
  43: complete local experiment, and the sharp recovery boundary, when two rates in
  44: a sampled generalized-Erlang renewal process collide?  At a double collision
  45: the labelled split disappears to first order.  Its identifiable coordinate is
  46: the squared half-separation, so root-\(N\) inference in that quotient becomes
  47: \(N^{-1/4}\) recovery of the unordered roots.  Theorems~F and G prove this for
  48: the actual stationary binary record, including renewal stopping and censored
  49: endpoint cycles, and match the estimation upper bound with a contiguity lower
  50: bound.
  51: 
  52: The original applied-probability question remains as the two-state instance:
  53: what the binary arrival record of a constrained D-MAP determines when every
  54: marked transition resets the hidden chain to a fixed state.  This reset creates
  55: renewal structure, while the usual nonuniqueness of Markovian and phase-type
  56: representations remains.  The model therefore sits at the intersection of
  57: renewal theory, D-MAP weak equivalence, phase-type representation, and singular
  58: stationary-record inference.
  59: 
  60: Our two-state parametrization has hidden states \(R\) and \(D\).  During a
  61: sampling interval of length \(\Delta\tau\), an attempt clock has rate
  62: \(\Gamma\) and a recovery clock has rate \(\kappa_{\mathrm r}\).  A marked
  63: transition is latched in \(D\) until the next boundary.  This construction is
  64: only a realization of the probability model: the results concern the labelled
  65: kernels and their visible binary law.  Allowing a marked transition into
  66: \(R\) changes the model and removes the deterministic regeneration used below.
  67: 
  68: Classical MAP and D-MAP theory supplies the arrival-process framework
  69: \cite{Neuts1979MAP,Lucantoni1991BMAP,AlfaNeuts1995DMAP}.  Zamparo's
  70: renewal-binary results supply the finite-dimensional renewal-law language and
  71: the finite-order Markov criterion used here \cite{Zamparo2022RenewalBinary}.
  72: Ram\'irez-Cobo and Lillo give the complete weak-equivalence classification for
  73: MAP2 and MAP3 processes \cite{RamirezCoboLillo2012WeakEquivalentMAP};
  74: M\'esz\'aros and Telek give canonical coordinates for discrete MAP2/RAP2
  75: models \cite{MeszarosTelek2013DiscreteMAP2Canonical}.  Those results are the
  76: primary comparison objects for both the quotient inverse and the killed-reset
  77: cone intersection.  The direct three-inclusion inverse below is a candidate
  78: original result pending complete reduction against canonical DMAP2
  79: coordinates.  It is not asserted as an established priority claim.

  82: theory are the primary antecedents \cite{HeZhang2008MinimalCoxian,
  83: HeZhang2009GeneralizedErlang}.  Our serial statement is limited to the

  85: poles.  For general killed-reset kernels, realization uniqueness identifies a
  86: similarity orbit, but only its intersection with the Markov cone consists of

 119: The specification statistic imports distributional-distance consistency from
 120: stationary-ergodic testing \cite{RyabkoRyabko2010ErgodicInference,
 121: Ryabko2012StationaryTesting}.  The physical-image statistic instead tests the
 122: finite-dimensional inclusion image under the sampled-counter model.  These are
 123: different questions, and neither diagnostic is used to select a model and then
 124: authorize another inferential statement from the same record.

 126: \begin{assumption}[Constrained sampled-counter D-MAP model]\label{ass:model-inference-contract-main}
 127: Fix \((\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)\in(0,\infty)^3\) and define
 128: \[
 129: p=e^{-\Gamma\Delta\tau},\qquad
 130: s=e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau},
 131: \]
 132: \[
 133: a=\int_0^{\Delta\tau}\kappa_{\mathrm r}e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}r}
 134: \bigl(1-e^{-\Gamma(\Delta\tau-r)}\bigr)\,dr,\qquad
 135: b=\int_0^{\Delta\tau}\kappa_{\mathrm r}e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}r}
 136: e^{-\Gamma(\Delta\tau-r)}\,dr .
 137: \]
 138: The record model is the two-state D-MAP with hidden states ordered as
 139: \((R,D)\) and labelled kernels
 140: \[
 141: T_0=\begin{pmatrix}p&0\\ b&s\end{pmatrix},
 142: \qquad
 143: T_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1-p\\0&a\end{pmatrix}.
 144: \]
 145: The convention is
 146: \((T_i)_{XY}=\PP(A_n=i,H_{n+1}=Y\mid H_n=X)\), the visible process
 147: \((A_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}\) is the stationary binary process generated by these
 148: kernels, and formulas on \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\) are interpreted by
 149: continuous limits.  The killed entries \(T_1(R,R)=T_1(D,R)=0\) are a structural
 150: constraint of this D-MAP, not optional boundary cases of the finite-record
 151: theorems.
 152: \end{assumption}
 153: 
 154: \subsection{Scope of finite-record reports}\label{subsec:finite-record-report-scope-main}
 155: 
 156: The retained-record limits are fixed-setting asymptotic statements inside the
 157: stationary law specified in \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}.  The
 158: model, population point, complete-cycle convention, and deterministic batch
 159: sequence are fixed before the record is interpreted.  Theorems~C and D are CLT
 160: and specification-test statements, respectively; Theorem~E is the quotient
 161: delta method.  The pointwise projection example is supplementary and has no
 162: confidence-set, testing, or coverage conclusion.
 163: 
 164: The only model interpretation assumed by this contract is the latched
 165: killed-leakage sampled-counter protocol of
 166: \Cref{lem:classical-counter-kernel-construction-main}.  If the sampling
 167: interval \(\Delta\tau\) is a known design interval, the visible stationary
 168: record identifies the unordered survival-factor set
 169: \(\{p,s\}=\{e^{-\Gamma\Delta\tau},e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau}\}\) and
 170: hence the unordered numerical rate set

+\subsection{Uniform score, stopping, plug-in, and two-point lemmas}
+\label{subsec:singular-uniform-lemmas-main}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform sampled-bin and sampled-tail derivatives]
+\label{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{U1}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\).  In addition,
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Compress the colliding holding times into \(Y=X_1+X_2\).  Relative to
+Lebesgue measure on \((0,\infty)^{n-1}\), the complete holding-time density is
+\[
+ f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)
+ =(c^2-\delta)e^{-cy}\frac{\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)}{\sqrt\delta}
+ \prod_{j=3}^n\theta_j e^{-\theta_jx_j},
+\tag{U2}
+\]
+where the quotient at \(\delta=0\) is \(y\).  Write
+\(\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)/\sqrt\delta=y h(\delta y^2)\), where
+\(h(x)=\sinh(\sqrt x)/\sqrt x\) is positive and analytic on
+\([0,\infty)\).  On a sufficiently small common neighbourhood,
+\(c^2-\delta\) and every rate are bounded away from zero.  The derivatives
+through order three of \(\log h(x)\) are bounded on \([0,\infty)\): they are
+continuous at zero by the power series, and their elementary hyperbolic
+expressions are bounded as \(x\to\infty\).  Differentiating \(\log f_q\)
+therefore gives, uniformly on \(\mathcal Q^+\),
+\[
+ |\partial_q^a\log f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)|
+ \le C_a\{1+(y+x_3+\cdots+x_n)^{2|a|}\},
+ \qquad 1\le |a|\le3.
+\tag{U3}
+\]
+
+Put \(W=Y+X_3+\cdots+X_n\).  Differentiation under the integral in a
+sampling bin expresses every derivative of \(\log g_q(k)\) through order
+three as a finite universal polynomial in conditional expectations of the
+complete-data derivatives in \textup{(U3)}, conditional on
+\(k\Delta\tau<W\le(k+1)\Delta\tau\).  On this event every nonnegative
+holding time is at most \((k+1)\Delta\tau\), which proves the first bound in
+\textup{(U1)}.  This argument controls the ratio by the bin probability
+itself and hence does not infer a relative bound from an absolute derivative
+bound.
+
+For the tail ratios, each exponential density is log-concave, convolution
+preserves log-concavity, and integration over a half-line shows that the
+survival function of \(W\) is log-concave.  Thus \(W\) is IFR and its residual
+life satisfies
+\[
+ \PP_q(W-t>x\mid W>t)\le \PP_q(W>x),\qquad t,x\ge0.
+\tag{U4}
+\]
+All rates on \(\mathcal Q^+\) exceed a common \(\underline\theta>0\), so
+\(W\) is stochastically dominated by an
+Erlang\((n,\underline\theta)\) variable.  Consequently, for every fixed
+integer \(m\),
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}\EE_q(W^m\mid W>t)
+ \le C_m(1+t)^m.
+\tag{U5}
+\]
+The same conditional-score polynomial argument, now conditional on
+\(W>k\Delta\tau\), proves the second bound in \textup{(U1)}.  Finally,
+stochastic domination by the Erlang variable gives the common
+polynomial-exponential mass envelope.  The envelopes justify every
+differentiation under the integral and continuity at \(\delta=0\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Uniform stopped renewal-score CLT and LLN]
+\label{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial age \(A_N\) and terminal residual \(R_N\), and put
+\(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in \(q\in\mathcal Q\), and also for
+triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),
+\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\tag{U6}
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous,
+\(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\tag{U7}
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\tag{U8}
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\(N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)\) uniformly.  These conclusions
+hold jointly and hence apply to the score, stopped Hessian, and third-order
+likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local triangular arrays.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The common exponential moment gives uniform bounds for every moment of
+\(D\), with \(0<\inf_q\mu_q\le\sup_q\mu_q<\infty\).  For the ordinary
+renewal count, compare the partial sums of \(D_j-\mu_q\) at
+\(\lfloor N/\mu_q\pm x\sqrt N\rfloor\).  Chebyshev's inequality and
+Kolmogorov's maximal inequality give a bound \(C/x^2\), uniformly in \(q\),
+for deviation of the count by more than \(x\sqrt N\).  The stationary delay
+changes this count only through the initial incomplete cycle, which is
+\(O_P(\log N)\) by the bound below.  This proves the first part of
+\textup{(U6)} without requiring independence between a reward and its cycle
+length.
+
+The equilibrium formula
+\(\PP_q(A_N\ge t)=\mu_q^{-1}\sum_{j\ge t}S_q(j)\), and its terminal analogue,
+have a common exponential-polynomial bound.  There are at most \(N\) complete
+gaps because \(D\ge1\).  A union bound for those gaps and the two endpoint
+variables therefore makes the probability that the maximum exceeds
+\(C_0\log N\) tend to zero uniformly for sufficiently large \(C_0\).  This
+proves the second part of \textup{(U6)}.
+
+For \(m_N=\lfloor N/\mu_q\rfloor\), the triangular-array Lindeberg theorem
+applied to the deterministic sum of \(b_q(G_j)\) gives the normal law in
+\textup{(U7)}.  The common polynomial envelope and exponential moment verify
+Lindeberg uniformly.  Replacing \(m_N\) by \(K_N\) changes the sum by at most
+the maximum of centred partial sums over \(O_P(\sqrt N)\) indices.
+Kolmogorov's inequality makes that difference \(o_P(\sqrt N)\) uniformly;
+this is the stopped-score, or Anscombe, step.  The same replacement in a
+law of large numbers is \(o_P(N)\), proving \textup{(U8)}.  The last assertion
+follows from \(K_N=O_P(N)\) and uniform integrability of the envelope.
+
+To verify the displayed uniformity rather than only pointwise convergence,
+take an arbitrary parameter sequence.  Compactness supplies a convergent
+subsequence; parameter continuity plus the common exponential envelope gives
+convergence of the means, covariance matrices, Lindeberg terms, and all LLN
+integrals along it.  The preceding inequalities have constants independent of
+the subsequence.  Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence with
+the asserted joint limits, which is the uniform subsequence criterion and
+also proves the triangular-array statement.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Efficient-score plug-in equicontinuity]
+\label{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\tag{U9}
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_{\eta}\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\tag{U10}
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Uniform nondegeneracy makes the projection coefficient in \textup{(U9)} twice
+continuously differentiable with polynomial score envelopes.  By construction,
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}\psi_\eta=0,
+ \qquad \EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U11}
+\]
+Differentiating the first identity, justified by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}, gives
+\[
+ \EE_{\eta,0}(\partial_\eta\psi_\eta)
+ =-\EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
+\tag{U12}
+\]
+Thus the derivative of \(\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}\) is a normalized stopped sum
+of centred rewards and is \(O_P(1)\) uniformly by
+\Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}.  A second-order Taylor expansion
+over a ball of radius \(L/\sqrt N\) has first term \(O_P(N^{-1/2})\); its
+second term is bounded by
+\(N^{-1/2}O_P(N)O(N^{-1})=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).  This proves \textup{(U10)}.
+The stopped LLN applied to score outer products, followed by the same Taylor
+bound and continuity of matrix inversion on the uniformly positive-definite
+set, proves information consistency.  The normalization and the two
+stationary endpoint scores obey the same conclusion: their parameter
+increments are bounded by \(N^{-1/2}\) times a polynomial in
+\(\max(A_N,R_N)\), which is \(O_P(\log N)\) by \textup{(U6)}.  Thus they
+contribute \(o_P(1)\) uniformly to the plug-in difference.  Contiguity
+transfers every null \(o_P(1)\) assertion to bounded local alternatives.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Two-point threshold-risk lower bound]
+\label{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}
+Fix a collision base \((\eta_0,0)\), hold \(\eta_0\) fixed, and compare
+\(P_{0,N}=P_{\eta_0,0}^{(N)}\) with
+\(P_{1,N}=P_{\eta_0,v_0/\sqrt N}^{(N)}\), where \(v_0>0\).  Let
+\(\mathcal R_{i,N}\) be their unordered rate multisets.  Then
+\[
+ d_{\rm m}(\mathcal R_{0,N},\mathcal R_{1,N})
+ =\sqrt{v_0}\,N^{-1/4},
+\tag{U13}
+\]
+and, for every \(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\),
+\[
+ \liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat{\mathcal R}_N}
+ \max_{i=0,1}P_{i,N}\!\left\{
+ N^{1/4}d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N,\mathcal R_{i,N})>a
+ \right\}
+ \ge \Phi_{\rm N}\!\left(
+ -\frac{v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}}2\right)>0.
+\tag{U14}
+\]
+Thus the lower conclusion is pointwise at a fixed base, uses two alternatives
+and threshold loss, and asserts optimality in rate rather than an exact
+minimax-risk theorem over a continuum of local parameters.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The two balls of radius \(aN^{-1/4}\) around the candidates are disjoint by
+\textup{(U13)}.  Assigning an estimate to its nearer candidate therefore
+turns simultaneous success of an estimator into correct testing of
+\(P_{0,N}\) against \(P_{1,N}\).  The LAN likelihood ratio under \(P_{0,N}\)
+converges to
+\[
+ \exp\{v_0Z-\tfrac12v_0^2I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)\},
+ \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)).
+\tag{U15}
+\]
+Its limit has mean one; mutual contiguity makes the likelihood ratios uniformly
+integrable, so their total-variation distances converge to that of the two
+Gaussian shifts separated by
+\(v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}\).  For any test, its maximum error is at
+least its equal-prior average error, whose limiting infimum is
+\(\Phi_{\rm N}\{-v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}/2\}\).  Taking a
+measurable estimator within \(o(1)\) of the infimum at each \(N\) proves
+\textup{(U14)}.  Strict positivity also follows directly from mutual
+contiguity, but \textup{(U14)} records the quantitative Gaussian bound.
+\end{proof}

+Finite-mixture singular rates and local minimax theory
+\cite{Chen1995FiniteMixtureRate,HoNguyen2019SingularityStructures,
+HeinrichKahn2018FiniteMixtureMinimax}. &
+Those works show in adjacent mixture models that root coalescence can slow
+parameter recovery, and that the rate depends on the model's singularity
+structure; in particular, \(N^{-1/4}\) is not a universal collision law. &
+They are antecedents for the singular-rate phenomenon, not sources of the
+present renewal theorem.  Here the quadratic coordinate and its information
+are derived from the exact stationary sampled-gap likelihood, and the upper
+rate is paired only with a fixed-base two-point threshold lower bound, not an
+exact minimax-risk constant. \\
+\addlinespace
+Confluent and near-colliding Prony recovery
+\cite{BatenkovYomdin2013ConfluentProny,
+AkinshinGoldmanYomdin2021NearCollidingProny}. &
+The sampled tail is a confluent exponential-polynomial sequence, so its
+annihilating recurrence inherits the established instability of recovering
+individual near-colliding roots. &
+This article does not claim to discover root-collision instability.  Its
+increment is to recover regular quotient coordinates through a measurable
+finite analytic atlas inside a stationary statistical experiment and to match
+the induced \(N^{-1/4}\) root rate with a statistical two-point lower bound. \\
+\addlinespace
+Jorgensen--Johnson LAN, information bounds, and efficient estimation for
+periodic nonparalyzable dead-time event-detection records
+\cite{JorgensenJohnson2026DED}. &
+Their non-i.i.d. binary record is generated by periodic gated dead-time event
+detection and has regular root-\(N\) parameters.  The present record instead
+resets at observed renewals and is reduced by stationary Palm inversion. &
+Their result is the closest dead-time LAN comparator, but it does not treat a
+generalized-Erlang double-rate collision.  The distinctions are renewal reset
+versus periodic gating, loss versus retention of first-order identifiability,
+and \(N^{-1/4}\) unordered collision recovery versus regular root-\(N\)
+estimation. \\
